data.name: Emulation.Emulator.azahar.Description
data.value: Emulates compatible Nintendo systems with Azahar.

data.name: Emulation.Option.azahar.citra_use_cpu_jit.Help
data.value: Enable Just-In-Time compilation for ARM CPU emulation. Significantly improves performance but may reduce accuracy. Restart required.

data.name: Emulation.Option.azahar.citra_cpu_clock_percentage.Help
data.value: Adjust the emulated 3DS CPU clock speed as a percentage of normal speed. Higher values may improve performance in some games but can cause issues. Lower values can help with games that run too fast.

data.name: Emulation.Option.azahar.citra_is_new_3ds.Help
data.value: Select whether to emulate the original 3DS or New 3DS. New 3DS has additional CPU power and memory, required for some games. Restart required.

data.name: Emulation.Option.azahar.citra_region_value.Help
data.value: Set the 3DS system region. Auto-select will choose based on the game. Some games are region-locked and require matching regions.

data.name: Emulation.Option.azahar.citra_language_value.Help
data.value: Set the system language for the emulated 3DS. This affects in-game text language when supported.

data.name: Emulation.Option.azahar.citra_audio_emulation.Help
data.value: Select audio emulation method. HLE is faster, LLE is more accurate.

data.name: Emulation.Option.azahar.citra_input_type.Help
data.value: Select how microphone input is handled for games that support it.

data.name: Emulation.Option.azahar.citra_graphics_api.Help
data.value: Select the graphics rendering API. Auto will choose the best available option. Restart required.

data.name: Emulation.Option.azahar.citra_use_hw_shader.Help
data.value: Use GPU hardware to accelerate shader processing. Significantly improves performance but may reduce accuracy.

data.name: Emulation.Option.azahar.citra_use_shader_jit.Help
data.value: Use Just-In-Time compilation for shaders. Improves performance but may cause graphical issues in some games.

data.name: Emulation.Option.azahar.citra_shaders_accurate_mul.Help
data.value: Use accurate multiplication in shaders. More accurate but can reduce performance. Only works with hardware shaders.

data.name: Emulation.Option.azahar.citra_use_disk_shader_cache.Help
data.value: Save compiled shaders to disk to reduce loading times on subsequent runs.

data.name: Emulation.Option.azahar.citra_resolution_factor.Help
data.value: Render the 3DS screens at a higher resolution. Higher values improve visual quality but significantly impact performance.

data.name: Emulation.Option.azahar.citra_texture_filter.Help
data.value: Apply texture filtering to enhance visual quality. Some filters may significantly impact performance.

data.name: Emulation.Option.azahar.citra_texture_sampling.Help
data.value: Control how textures are sampled and filtered.

data.name: Emulation.Option.azahar.citra_custom_textures.Help
data.value: Enable loading of custom texture packs to replace original game textures.

data.name: Emulation.Option.azahar.citra_dump_textures.Help
data.value: Save original game textures to disk for creating custom texture packs. May impact performance.

data.name: Emulation.Option.azahar.citra_layout_option.Help
data.value: Choose how the 3DS screens are arranged in the display.

data.name: Emulation.Option.azahar.citra_swap_screen.Help
data.value: Choose which screen is displayed prominently in single screen or large screen layouts.

data.name: Emulation.Option.azahar.citra_swap_screen_mode.Help
data.value: How screen swapping behaves when using the screen swap hotkey.

data.name: Emulation.Option.azahar.citra_large_screen_proportion.Help
data.value: How many times larger the main screen is compared to the small screen in the Large Screen layout.

data.name: Emulation.Option.azahar.citra_render_3d.Help
data.value: Stereoscopic 3D output, used when a game is rendering in 3D. 'Off' shows a single 2D image. 'Side by Side' places the left and right eye images beside each other in one frame, each at half width. 'Side by Side (Full)' does the same but keeps each eye at full width. 'Anaglyph' merges both eyes into a single red/cyan image for use with red/cyan glasses. 'Interlaced' alternates the eyes on odd and even scanlines for interlaced 3D displays, and 'Reverse Interlaced' swaps which eye is on which line. 'Cardboard VR' outputs side by side with lens-distortion correction for Cardboard-style viewers.

data.name: Emulation.Option.azahar.citra_factor_3d.Help
data.value: Depth intensity of the stereoscopic 3D effect, as a percentage. Only used when a 3D mode is active.

data.name: Emulation.Option.azahar.citra_use_virtual_sd.Help
data.value: Enable virtual SD card support for homebrew and some commercial games.

data.name: Emulation.Option.azahar.citra_use_libretro_save_path.Help
data.value: Choose where save data and system files are stored.

data.name: Emulation.Option.azahar.citra_analog_function.Help
data.value: Configure what the right analog stick controls.

data.name: Emulation.Option.azahar.citra_analog_deadzone.Help
data.value: Set the deadzone percentage for analog input to reduce drift.

data.name: Emulation.Option.azahar.citra_enable_mouse_touchscreen.Help
data.value: Enable mouse input for touchscreen interactions.

data.name: Emulation.Option.azahar.citra_enable_touch_touchscreen.Help
data.value: Enable touch device input for touchscreen interactions.

data.name: Emulation.Option.azahar.citra_enable_touch_pointer_timeout.Help
data.value: Whether or not the touchscreen pointer should disappear during inactivity.

data.name: Emulation.Option.azahar.citra_enable_motion.Help
data.value: Enable gyroscope and accelerometer input for games that support motion controls.

data.name: Emulation.Option.citra.citra_use_hw_shader_cache
data.value: Save hardware shader cache to disk

data.name: Emulation.Option.citra.citra_use_acc_geo_shaders
data.value: Enable accurate geometry shaders (only for H/W shaders)

data.name: Emulation.Option.citra.citra_use_acc_mul
data.value: Enable accurate shaders multiplication (only for H/W shaders)

data.name: Emulation.Option.citra2018.citra2018_use_acc_geo_shaders

data.name: Emulation.Emulator.desmume.Description

data.name: Emulation.Option.desmume.desmume_firmware_language.Help
data.value: Set language to use for firmware.

data.name: Emulation.Option.desmume.desmume_use_external_bios.Help
data.value: Use official BIOS. Core needs to be restarted for changes to apply.

data.name: Emulation.Option.desmume.desmume_boot_into_bios
data.value: Boot Into BIOS (interpreter and external bios only)

data.name: Emulation.Option.desmume.desmume_load_to_memory.Help
data.value: Load the game into memory to reduce IO lag.

data.name: Emulation.Option.desmume.desmume_num_cores.Help
data.value: Set the amount of CPU cores to use.

data.name: Emulation.Option.desmume.desmume_cpu_mode.Help
data.value: Enable or disable the use of the dynamic recompiler.

data.name: Emulation.Option.desmume.desmume_jit_block_size.Help
data.value: Set the block size of the JIT dynamic recompiler.

data.name: Emulation.Option.desmume.desmume_advanced_timing.Help
data.value: Enables the use of Advanced Bus-Level Timing.

data.name: Emulation.Option.desmume.desmume_frameskip.Help
data.value: Sets the amount of frames to skip.

data.name: Emulation.Option.desmume.desmume_internal_resolution.Help
data.value: Sets the internal resolution. Higher resolutions can provide better clarity for 3D scenes & objects, but will increase the performance requirements

data.name: Emulation.Option.desmume.desmume_color_depth.Help
data.value: Sets the Color Depth to either 16-bit or 32-bit colors. Requires the OpenGL Rasterizer.

data.name: Emulation.Option.desmume.desmume_gfx_multisampling.Help
data.value: Set the multiplier for Multisampling Anti Aliasing. Requires the OpenGL Rasterizer.

data.name: Emulation.Option.desmume.desmume_gfx_texture_smoothing.Help
data.value: Enables Texture Smoothing. Requires the OpenGL Rasterizer.

data.name: Emulation.Option.desmume.desmume_opengl_shadow_polygon.Help
data.value: Enables Shadow Polygons. Requires the OpenGL Rasterizer.

data.name: Emulation.Option.desmume.desmume_opengl_special_zero_alpha.Help
data.value: Enables Special 0 Alpha. Requires the OpenGL Rasterizer.

data.name: Emulation.Option.desmume.desmume_opengl_nds_depth_calculation.Help
data.value: Enables NDS Depth Calculation. Requires the OpenGL Rasterizer.

data.name: Emulation.Option.desmume.desmume_opengl_depth_lequal_polygon_facing.Help
data.value: Enables Depth-LEqual Polygon Facing. Requires the OpenGL Rasterizer.

data.name: Emulation.Option.desmume.desmume_gfx_texture_scaling.Help
data.value: Sets the multiplier for xBrz texture scaling to use.

data.name: Emulation.Option.desmume.desmume_screens_layout.Help
data.value: Select the screen layout to use.

data.name: Emulation.Option.desmume.desmume_screens_gap.Help
data.value: Sets the amout of space between the top and bottom screens.

data.name: Emulation.Option.desmume.desmume_hybrid_layout_ratio.Help
data.value: Sets the screen ratio for the hybrid screen(s) to use.

data.name: Emulation.Option.desmume.desmume_hybrid_layout_scale
data.value: Hybrid Layout: Scale So Small Screen is 1:1px

data.name: Emulation.Option.desmume.desmume_hybrid_layout_scale.Help
data.value: Force the small screen to render at 1:1px.

data.name: Emulation.Option.desmume.desmume_hybrid_showboth_screens.Help
data.value: Show both top & bottom small screens.

data.name: Emulation.Option.desmume.desmume_hybrid_cursor_always_smallscreen
data.value: Hybrid Layout: Cursor Always on Small Screen

data.name: Emulation.Option.desmume.desmume_hybrid_cursor_always_smallscreen.Help
data.value: Only display the cursor on the small bottom screen.

data.name: Emulation.Option.desmume.desmume_pointer_type.Help
data.value: Select what type of input to use for the pointer.

data.name: Emulation.Option.desmume.desmume_mouse_speed.Help
data.value: Sets the speed multiplier to use for the mouse pointer.

data.name: Emulation.Option.desmume.desmume_input_rotation.Help
data.value: Sets the rotation of the pointer.

data.name: Emulation.Option.desmume.desmume_pointer_device_l.Help
data.value: Sets the pointer mode for the left analog stick.

data.name: Emulation.Option.desmume.desmume_pointer_device_r.Help
data.value: Sets the pointer mode for the right analog stick.

data.name: Emulation.Option.desmume.desmume_pointer_device_deadzone.Help
data.value: Sets the stick deadzone for the emulated pointer.

data.name: Emulation.Option.desmume.desmume_pointer_device_acceleration_mod.Help
data.value: Sets the percent for the Pointer Acceleration Modifier.

data.name: Emulation.Option.desmume.desmume_pointer_stylus_pressure.Help
data.value: Sets the percent for the Emulated Stylus Pressure Modifier.

data.name: Emulation.Option.desmume.desmume_pointer_colour.Help
data.value: Sets what color to use for the pointer.

data.name: Emulation.Option.desmume.desmume_mic_mode.Help
data.value: Sets what type of noise to use when pressing the microfone button.

data.value: Hybrid layout cursor always on small screen

data.name: Emulation.Option.melonds.melonds_boot_directly.Help
data.value: Choose if the core should boot the game directly or if it should boot to the DS menu instead (BIOS and firmware files required).

data.name: Emulation.Option.melonds.melonds_use_fw_settings.Help
data.value: Use language and username from the DS firmware. When disabled or if firmware file was not found, the username will be provided by the Libretro frontend, if it's empty it will default to 'melonDS'.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melonds.melonds_language.Help
data.value: Selected language will be used if 'Use Firmware Settings' is disabled or if firmware file was not found.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melonds.melonds_mic_input.Help
data.value: Choose the type of noise that will be used as microphone input.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melonds.melonds_touch_mode.Help
data.value: Choose mode for interactions with the touch screen.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melonds.melonds_swapscreen_mode.Help
data.value: Choose if the 'Swap screens' button should work on press or on hold.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melonds.melonds_screen_layout.Help
data.value: Choose how many screens should be displayed and how they should be displayed.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melonds.melonds_screen_gap.Help
data.value: Choose how large the gap between the 2 screens should be.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melonds.melonds_hybrid_small_screen.Help

data.name: Emulation.Emulator.melondsds.Description
data.value: Emulates compatible Nintendo systems with melonDS DS.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_mic_input.Help
data.value:
Choose the sound that the emulated microphone will receive:
Silence: No audio input. Blow: Loop a built-in blowing sound. Noise: Random white noise. Microphone: Use your real microphone if available, fall back to Silence if not.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_mic_input_active.Help
data.value:
Set the behavior of the Microphone button, even if Microphone Input Mode is set to Blow or Noise. The emulated microphone receives silence when disabled by the button.
Hold: Button enables mic input while held. Toggle: Button enables mic input when pressed, disables it when pressed again. Always: Button is ignored, mic input is always enabled.
Ignored if Microphone Input Mode is set to Silence.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_audio_bitdepth.Help
data.value: The number of bits used for each audio sample. Automatic matches the original hardware's behavior by using 10-bit audio for DS mode and 16-bit audio for DSi mode. If unsure, set to Automatic.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_audio_interpolation.Help
data.value: Interpolates audio output for improved quality. Disable this to match the behavior of the original DS hardware.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_jit_enable.Help
data.value: Recompiles emulated machine code into native code as it runs, considerably improving performance over plain interpretation. Takes effect at next restart. If unsure, leave enabled.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_jit_fast_memory.Help
data.value: Disable this if running melonDS DS through a debugger, otherwise the constant (but expected) SIGSEGVs will get annoying. Takes effect at next restart. If unsure, leave enabled.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_firmware_wfc_dns.Help
data.value:
The DNS server to use for the emulated access point ("melonAP"). Use this to play online with custom servers that reimplement the discontinued Nintendo Wi-Fi Connection services. Game support depends on the server. Some internet service providers may block requests to these servers. If this is the case for you, see https://tinyurl.com/393cb755 for a workaround.
The listed servers are not affiliated with libretro, Nintendo, the melonDS team, or this core's author. Please respect other players and follow the server's rules.
If unsure, leave on Kaeru WFC. Changes take effect at next restart.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_firmware_language.Help
data.value:
Overrides the language mode of the emulated console.
Use Host: Uses the frontend's language if supported by the console. Don't Override: Use whatever language is already set on the firmware. This is the fallback behavior if the emulated DS (or DSi NAND) doesn't support the frontend's language.
Not every game honors this setting. Changes take effect at next restart.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_firmware_username.Help
data.value:
Overrides the username given to the emulated console.
Don't Override: Uses whatever name is defined on the firmware. Guess: Try to get your username from the frontend. If that fails, try the USER, USERNAME, and LOGNAME environment variables. melonDS DS: Uses "melonDS DS". This is the default if nothing else works.
Names are truncated to 10 characters. Changes take effect at next restart.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_firmware_favorite_color.Help
data.value: The theme ("favorite color") of the emulated console. Changes take effect at next restart.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_firmware_birth_month.Help
data.value: The month of your birthday. Changes take effect at next restart.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_firmware_birth_day.Help
data.value: The day within the month of your birthday. Changes take effect at next restart.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_firmware_enable_alarm.Help
data.value: Whether the emulated console's alarm is enabled. Changes take effect at next restart.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_firmware_alarm_hour.Help
data.value: The hour of the configured alarm. Changes take effect at next restart.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_firmware_alarm_minute.Help
data.value: The minute of the configured alarm. Changes take effect at next restart.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_network_mode.Help
data.value:
Configures how melonDS DS emulates Nintendo WFC. If unsure, use Indirect mode.
Indirect: Use libslirp to emulate the DS's network stack. Simple and needs no setup. Direct: Routes emulated Wi-Fi packets to the host's network interface. Faster and more reliable, but requires an ethernet connection and that WinPcap or Npcap is installed. that libpcap is installed. If unavailable, falls back to Indirect mode.
Changes take effect at next restart. Not related to local multiplayer.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_direct_network_interface.Help
data.value: Select a network interface to use with Direct Mode. If unsure, set to Automatic. Changes take effect at next core restart.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_mac_address_mode.Help
data.value: Configures how the emulated console's MAC address is set. Changing this option might make local multiplayer impossible or block access to save files in games that use the MAC address to prevent tampering of save files (i.e. Pokémon). No relation to the direct mode interface. Changes take effect at next restart. See https://bit.ly/4fJtWKN for more information.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_show_unsupported_features.Help
data.value: Enable to display an on-screen message if melonDS tries to use certain unsupported features. These warnings will be logged regardless of this setting.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_show_bios_warnings.Help
data.value: Enable to display warnings if your BIOS files have certain known problems. A warning will always be shown if your BIOS files are missing or invalid, regardless of this setting.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_show_current_layout.Help
data.value: Enable to show which screen layout within the configured sequence is active.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_show_mic_state.Help
data.value: Enable to show whether your device's microphone is active.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_show_camera_state.Help
data.value: Enable to show whether your device's camera is active.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_show_lid_state.Help
data.value: Enable to show whether the emulated screens are closed.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_show_sensor_reading.Help
data.value: Enable to show the emulated input of any peripheral sensors that aren't already managed by one of the other OSD options, e.g. the solar sensor embedded in the Boktai trilogy's carts. If no peripherals (including GBA carts) are available, this option will have no effect.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_show_pointer_coordinates.Help
data.value: Enable to display the coordinates of the pointer within the touch screen. Used for debugging. Leave disabled if unsure.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_show_cursor.Help
data.value: Determines when a cursor should appear on the bottom screen. Never is recommended for touch screens; the other settings are best suited for mouse or joystick input.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_cursor_timeout.Help
data.value: If Cursor Mode is set to "Until Timeout", then the cursor will be hidden if it hasn't been moved for a certain time.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_touch_mode.Help
data.value:
Determines how the console's touch screen is emulated.
Joystick: Use a joystick to control the cursor. Recommended if you don't have a mouse or a real touch screen available. Pointer: Use your mouse or touch screen to control the cursor. Auto: Use either Joystick or Pointer, depending on which you last touched.
If unsure, set to Auto.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_joystick_cursor_deadzone.Help
data.value: If the joystick is within this deadzone the cursor will not move.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_joystick_cursor_maxspeed.Help
data.value: Set the max speed for the joystick cursor.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_joystick_cursor_response.Help
data.value: Set the response curve for the joystick cursor. Linear is a response curve where the cursor speed is 1:1 with the joystick input. Quadratic is a response curve that reduces the sensitivity near the joystick center for finer control, but increases the sensitivity near the edges

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_joystick_cursor_speedup.Help
data.value: Set the multiplier for the joystick cursor when the speedup/slowdown pointer button (L2 by default) is held

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_hybrid_ratio.Help
data.value: The size of the larger screen relative to the smaller ones when using a hybrid or largescreen layout.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_hybrid_small_screen.Help
data.value: Choose which screens will be shown when using a hybrid layout.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_opengl_filtering.Help
data.value:
Affects how the hybrid/largescreen screen is scaled up.
Nearest: No filtering. Graphics look blocky. Linear: Smooth scaling.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_screen_gap.Help
data.value: Choose how large the gap between the screens should be. Vertical layouts (including rotations) only. Dimensions exclude the effects of the frontend's scaling.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_secondary_screen_scale.Help
data.value: The size of the secondary screen relative to the primary screen. Applies to vertical layouts (Top/Bottom, Bottom/Top). At 100%, both screens are the same size. At 50%, the secondary screen is half the width and height of the primary screen.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_secondary_screen_filtering.Help
data.value:
Affects how the secondary screen is scaled down.
Nearest: No filtering. Graphics look blocky. Linear: Smooth scaling. Recommended when using Secondary Screen Scale below 100%.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_number_of_screen_layouts.Help
data.value: The number of screen layouts to cycle through with the Next Layout button.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_console_mode.Help
data.value:
Whether to emulate a Nintendo DS or a Nintendo DSi.
Auto uses DSi mode for games that need a DSi, and DS mode for everything else. The DS and DSi settings force the corresponding console; this is mostly useful for homebrew development.
DSi mode has some limits:
- Native BIOS/firmware/NAND files must be provided, including for the regular DS. - Some features (such as savestates) are not available in DSi mode.
See the DSi-specific options in this category for more information. If unsure, use Auto. Changes take effect at the next restart.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_sysfile_mode.Help
data.value:
Determines whether melonDS uses native BIOS/firmware dumps or its own built-in replacements. Only applies to DS mode, as DSi mode always requires native BIOS and firmware dumps.
Native mode uses BIOS and firmware files from a real DS. Place your dumps of these in the system directory or its "melonDS DS" subdirectory and name them as follows:
- DS BIOS: bios7.bin, bios9.bin - DSi BIOS: dsi_bios7.bin, dsi_bios9.bin - Firmware: See the "DS Firmware" and "DSi Firmware" options. - DSi NAND: See the "DSi NAND " option.
Falls back to Built-In if any BIOS/firmware file isn't found.
Built-In mode uses melonDS's built-in BIOS and firmware, and is suitable for most games.
Changes take effect at next restart.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_firmware_nds_path.Help
data.value:
Select a firmware image to use for DS mode. Files are listed here if they:
- Are inside the frontend's system directory, or a subdirectory named "melonDS DS". - Are exactly 131,072 bytes (128KB), 262,144 bytes (256KB), or 524,288 bytes (512KB) long. - Contain valid header data for DS firmware.
Nintendo WFC IDs are saved to firmware, so switching firmware images may result in the loss of some WFC data. Ignored in DSi mode or if BIOS/Firmware Mode is Built-In. Changes take effect at next restart.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_firmware_dsi_path.Help
data.value:
Select a firmware image to use for DSi mode. Files are listed here if they:
- Are inside the frontend's system directory, or a subdirectory named "melonDS DS". - Are exactly 131,072 bytes (128KB), 262,144 bytes (256KB), or 524,288 bytes (512KB) long. - Contain valid header data for DSi firmware.
Nintendo WFC IDs are saved to firmware, so switching firmware images may result in the loss of some WFC data. Changes take effect at next restart.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_dsi_nand_path.Help
data.value:
Select a DSi NAND image to use. Required when using DSi mode. Files are listed here if they:
- Are inside the frontend's system directory, or a subdirectory named "melonDS DS". - Are exactly 251,658,304 bytes (240MB) or 257,425,472 bytes (245.5MB) long with valid footer data, OR; - Are 64 bytes shorter than these lengths and contain equivalent data at file offset 0xFF800.
Set to "Auto" to let the core pick a NAND image whose region matches the loaded DSiWare ROM. Changes take effect at next restart.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_boot_mode.Help
data.value:
Determines how melonDS boots games.
Native: Load games through the system menu, similar to the real DS/DSi boot process. Requires native BIOS and firmware files in the system directory. Direct: Skip the system menu and go straight to the game. Supported for DSiWare if native DSi system files are available.
Ignored if loaded without a game (Native is forced) or if using Built-In BIOS/Firmware (Direct is forced). Changes take effect at next restart.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_dsi_sdcard.Help
data.value: If enabled, a virtual SD card will be made available to the emulated DSi. The card image must be within the frontend's system directory and be named dsi_sd_card.bin. If no image exists, a 4GB virtual SD card will be created. Ignored in DS mode. Changes take effect at next boot.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_dsi_sdcard_readonly.Help
data.value: If enabled, the emulated DSi sees the virtual SD card as read-only. Changes take effect with next restart.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_dsi_sdcard_sync_sdcard_to_host.Help
data.value: If enabled, the virtual SD card's files will be synced to this core's save directory. Enable this if you want to add files to the virtual SD card from outside the core. Syncing happens when loading and unloading a game, so external changes won't have any effect while the core is running. Takes effect at the next boot. Adjusting this setting may overwrite existing save data.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_homebrew_sdcard.Help
data.value: If enabled, a virtual SD card will be made available to homebrew DS games. The card image must be within the frontend's system directory and be named dldi_sd_card.bin. If no image exists, a 4GB virtual SD card will be created. Ignored for retail games. Changes take effect at next boot.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_homebrew_readonly.Help
data.value: If enabled, homebrew applications will see the virtual SD card as read-only. Changes take effect with next restart.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_homebrew_sync_sdcard_to_host.Help
data.value: If enabled, the virtual SD card's files will be synced to this core's save directory. Enable this if you want to add files to the virtual SD card from outside the core. Syncing happens when loading and unloading a game, so external changes won't have any effect while the core is running. Takes effect at the next boot. Adjusting this setting may overwrite existing save data.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_battery_update_interval.Help
data.value: How often the emulated console's battery should be updated. Ignored if the frontend can't get the device's battery level.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_ds_battery_ok_threshold.Help
data.value: If the host's battery level falls below this percentage, the emulated DS will report that its battery level is low. Ignored if running in DSi mode, no battery is available, or the frontend can't query the power status.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_slot2_device.Help
data.value: The peripheral that will be inserted into the emulated console's Slot-2. Ignored in DSi mode, or if a GBA ROM is explicitly loaded. If a GBA ROM for any game in the Boktai trilogy is inserted, the corresponding Solar Sensor setting will be forced. In supported NDS games, each Boktai cart will have different effects. The Motion Paks read your device's accelerometer (and its gyroscope, for the homebrew pak) if the frontend supports them; otherwise, they act as if the console is lying flat and still. Changes take effect at next core start.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_rumble_intensity.Help
data.value:
How hard the Rumble Pak drives your controller's motors. The emulated Rumble Pak has no volume control of its own, so this scales whatever the game asks for.
Ignored unless "Slot-2 Device" is set to Rumble Pak.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_rumble_type.Help
data.value:
Which of your controller's motors the Rumble Pak drives. Most controllers pair a heavy motor with a lighter one; which feels closer to a real Rumble Pak depends on the controller.
Ignored unless "Slot-2 Device" is set to Rumble Pak.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_solar_sensor_host_sensor.Help
data.value:
If enabled, the emulated solar sensor's light input will come from your device's real luminance sensor if available. If disabled or no sensor is available, the emulated sensor can be manually controlled with the following button combos:
- L+A+Up or L+A+Down - Select+Up or Select+Down - Your mouse wheel
Ignored unless "Slot-2 Device" is set to Solar Sensor, or if a ROM for any game in the Boktai trilogy (any region) is inserted in the emulated console's Slot-2. If unsure, leave enabled.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_start_time_mode.Help
data.value:
The initial time of the emulated console's internal clock.
- Real: Start in sync with your device's clock. - Synchronized: Synchronize the emulated clock to your device's clock. May cause unexpected behavior in some games when rewinding or fast-forwarding. - Relative: Start in sync with your device's clock, plus or minus a specified offset. Will be constrained to dates that the DS can represent. - Absolute: Start at a specific date and time, regardless of your device's clock.
All dates and times are in your local timezone. Changes take effect at next restart.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_start_time_relative_year_offset.Help
data.value: The number of years to offset the starting time by. Only used when Starting Time Mode is Relative. Changes take effect at next restart.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_start_time_relative_day_offset.Help
data.value: The number of days to offset the starting time by. Only used when Starting Time Mode is Relative. Changes take effect at next restart.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_start_time_relative_hour_offset.Help
data.value: The number of hours to offset the starting time by. Only used when Starting Time Mode is Relative. Changes take effect at next restart.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_start_time_relative_minute_offset.Help
data.value: The number of minutes to offset the starting time by. Only used when Starting Time Mode is Relative. Changes take effect at next restart.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_start_time_absolute_year.Help
data.value: The initial year to use when Starting Time Mode is Absolute. Changes take effect at next restart.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_start_time_absolute_month.Help
data.value: The initial month to use when Starting Time Mode is Absolute. Changes take effect at next restart.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_start_time_absolute_day.Help
data.value: The initial day of the month to use when Starting Time Mode is Absolute. Days that extend past the end of a month will roll over to the next (e.g. April 31st will become May 1st). Changes take effect at next restart.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_start_time_absolute_hour.Help
data.value: The initial hour to use when Starting Time Mode is Absolute. Changes take effect at next restart.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_start_time_absolute_minute.Help
data.value: The initial minute to use when Starting Time Mode is Absolute. Changes take effect at next restart.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_start_time_absolute_second.Help
data.value: The initial second to use when Starting Time Mode is Absolute. Changes take effect at next restart.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_render_mode.Help
data.value:
Software is fastest and most accurate. OpenGL (Classic) can scale up 3D graphics, but some games don't render correctly. OpenGL (Compute) is accurate and supports upscaling, but won't work on some older devices. Switching to it takes a few seconds to compile its shaders.
Falls back to software rendering if OpenGL can't be used. Changes take effect immediately but may require the frontend's video driver to be restarted.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_opengl_resolution.Help
data.value: The degree to which the emulated 3D engine's graphics are scaled up. Dimensions are given per screen. OpenGL renderers only. Changing this takes a few seconds while the OpenGL (Compute) renderer recompiles its shaders.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_opengl_better_polygons.Help
data.value: Enable this if your game's 3D models are not rendering correctly. OpenGL (Classic) renderer only.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_compute_hires_coordinates.Help
data.value: Positions 3D geometry at the upscaled resolution instead of snapping it to the DS's native pixel grid, which smooths out wobbling polygons. A few games rely on the native grid and look wrong with this enabled. OpenGL (Compute) renderer only. Changing this takes a few seconds while the shaders are recompiled.

data.name: Emulation.Option.melondsds.melonds_threaded_renderer.Help
data.value: If enabled, the software renderer will run on a separate thread. Changes take effect immediately. If unsure, leave this enabled.

data.name: Emulation.Emulator.noods.Description
data.value: Emulates compatible Nintendo systems with NooDS.

data.name: Emulation.Emulator.skyemu.Description
data.value: Emulates compatible Nintendo systems with SkyEmu.

data.name: Emulation.Emulator.fceumm.Description
data.value: Emulates compatible Nintendo systems with FCEUmm.

data.name: Emulation.Option.fceumm.fceumm_region.Help
data.value: Force core to use NTSC, PAL or Dendy region timings.

data.name: Emulation.Option.fceumm.fceumm_game_genie.Help
data.value: Enable emulation of a Game Genie add-on cartridge, allowing cheat codes to be entered when launching games. The Game Genie ROM file 'gamegenie.nes' must be present in the frontend's system directory. Does not apply to FDS or arcade content.

data.name: Emulation.Option.fceumm.fceumm_show_adv_system_options.Help
data.value: Show advanced system options and tweaks.

data.name: Emulation.Option.fceumm.fceumm_show_adv_sound_options.Help
data.value: Show advanced sound options and tweaks.

data.name: Emulation.Option.fceumm.fceumm_overscan_h_left.Help
data.value: Removes pixels from left side of the screen to simulate overscan seen on standard CRT televisions.

data.name: Emulation.Option.fceumm.fceumm_overscan_h_right.Help
data.value: Removes pixels from right side of the screen to simulate overscan seen on standard CRT televisions.

data.name: Emulation.Option.fceumm.fceumm_overscan_v_top.Help
data.value: Removes pixels from the top of the screen to simulate overscan seen on standard CRT televisions.

data.name: Emulation.Option.fceumm.fceumm_overscan_v_bottom.Help
data.value: Removes pixels from the bottom of the screen to simulate overscan seen on standard CRT televisions.

data.name: Emulation.Option.fceumm.fceumm_palette.Help
data.value: Choose from pre-generated palettes, a custom 64x3 palette from file or raw format (needs to use a nes-decoder shader).

data.name: Emulation.Option.fceumm.fceumm_ntsc_filter.Help
data.value: Blargg's NTSC filters are used to replicate RF, Composite, S-Video, and RGB cable signals.

data.name: Emulation.Option.fceumm.fceumm_hdpacks.Help
data.value: Load Mesen-format HD texture packs from '<system>/HdPacks/<rom name>/hires.txt' when present. Replaces tiles/sprites with high-resolution artwork (PNG, DDS or WebP) and enables the pack's custom backgrounds and OGG/WAV music and sound effects. Requires a frontend that supports XRGB8888 output.

data.name: Emulation.Option.fceumm.fceumm_sndrate_hint.Help
data.value: The NES has no sample-based audio hardware; sound is synthesized in realtime, so there is no fixed output samplerate. Select the rate the core generates audio at. Higher rates lower latency and reduce aliasing and low-pass 'smearing' from frontend resampling, at a small performance cost. 'Auto' picks whichever supported rate is closest to the frontend's target output rate.

data.name: Emulation.Option.fceumm.fceumm_sndquality.Help
data.value: Enable higher quality sound. Increases performance requirements.

data.name: Emulation.Option.fceumm.fceumm_sndlowpass.Help
data.value: Apply a low pass audio filter to simulate the 'muted' sound of the NES when connected to a television via the RF modulator.

data.name: Emulation.Option.fceumm.fceumm_removetrianglenoise.Help
data.value: Mute the triangle channel when its period drops into the ultrasonic range (period <= 3, > ~12 kHz at NTSC). Eliminates the audible popping some games (Castlevania II: Simon's Quest, Jackal, etc.) produce in High / Very High sound quality, where the DAC reconstruction filter would otherwise fold the ultrasonic content back into the audible range. Low quality is unaffected (it already silences ultrasonic triangle output).

data.name: Emulation.Option.fceumm.fceumm_reducedmcpopping.Help
data.value: Smooth direct writes to the DMC DAC register ($4011) by stepping the DAC only halfway toward each new value. Reduces the audible click when games (Castlevania II: Simon's Quest, etc.) pulse the DAC for manual sample playback. Normal DPCM bit-stream sample playback is unaffected.

data.name: Emulation.Option.fceumm.fceumm_sndstereodelay.Help
data.value: Enable a fake stereo sound effect by delaying the right audio channel when upmixing the mono signal output from the NES.

data.name: Emulation.Option.fceumm.fceumm_swapduty.Help
data.value: Simulates the sound from famiclones that have the pulse wave channels duty cycle bits reversed.

data.name: Emulation.Option.fceumm.fceumm_apu_1.Help
data.value: Enables or disables pulse wave generator audio output 1.

data.name: Emulation.Option.fceumm.fceumm_apu_2.Help
data.value: Enables or disables pulse wave generator audio output 2.

data.name: Emulation.Option.fceumm.fceumm_apu_3.Help
data.value: Enables or disables triangle wave generator audio output.

data.name: Emulation.Option.fceumm.fceumm_apu_4.Help
data.value: Enables or disables noise generator audio output.

data.name: Emulation.Option.fceumm.fceumm_apu_5.Help
data.value: Enables or disables delta modulation channel audio output.

data.name: Emulation.Option.fceumm.fceumm_apu_fds.Help
data.value: Scale Famicom Disk System 2C33 wavetable expansion-audio output (0 = mute, 100 = unscaled).

data.name: Emulation.Option.fceumm.fceumm_apu_s5b.Help
data.value: Scale Sunsoft 5B (YM2149F) expansion-audio output (0 = mute, 100 = unscaled).

data.name: Emulation.Option.fceumm.fceumm_apu_n163.Help
data.value: Scale Namco 163 expansion-audio output (0 = mute, 100 = unscaled).

data.name: Emulation.Option.fceumm.fceumm_apu_vrc6.Help
data.value: Scale Konami VRC6 expansion-audio output (0 = mute, 100 = unscaled).

data.name: Emulation.Option.fceumm.fceumm_apu_vrc7.Help
data.value: Scale Konami VRC7 (YM2413-clone) expansion-audio output (0 = mute, 100 = unscaled).

data.name: Emulation.Option.fceumm.fceumm_apu_mmc5.Help
data.value: Scale Nintendo MMC5 PCM + square expansion-audio output (0 = mute, 100 = unscaled).

data.name: Emulation.Option.fceumm.fceumm_turbo_delay.Help
data.value: Repeat rate of turbo buttons in frames.

data.name: Emulation.Option.fceumm.fceumm_zapper_mode.Help
data.value: Selects device to use for Zapper games.

data.name: Emulation.Option.fceumm.fceumm_show_crosshair.Help
data.value: Shows or hides on-screen crosshairs when using a Zapper.

data.name: Emulation.Option.fceumm.fceumm_zapper_tolerance.Help
data.value: Sets how many pixels from target area is on target.

data.name: Emulation.Option.fceumm.fceumm_zapper_trigger.Help
data.value: Inverts trigger logic when using a Zapper. Disabling it resembles original hardware behavior.

data.name: Emulation.Option.fceumm.fceumm_zapper_sensor.Help
data.value: Inverts sensor logic when using a Zapper (Sequential Targets Light gun mode only). Disabling it resembles original NES/FC hardware behavior.

data.name: Emulation.Option.fceumm.fceumm_arkanoid_mode.Help
data.value: Selects device to use for Arkanoid games.

data.name: Emulation.Option.fceumm.fceumm_up_down_allowed.Help
data.value: Allows simultaneous UP+DOWN or LEFT+RIGHT button combinations, which can create different effects in some games.

data.name: Emulation.Option.fceumm.fceumm_nospritelimit.Help
data.value: Removes the 8-per-scanline hardware limit. This reduces sprite flickering but can cause some games to glitch since some use this for effects.

data.name: Emulation.Option.fceumm.fceumm_overclocking.Help
data.value: Enables or disables overclocking, which can reduce slowdowns in some games. Postrender method is more compatible with every game, Vblank is more effective for games like Contra Force.

data.name: Emulation.Option.fceumm.fceumm_ramstate.Help
data.value: RAM values on power up. Some games rely on initial RAM values for random number generation as an example.

data.name: Emulation.Emulator.fixnes.Description
data.value: Emulates compatible Nintendo systems with fixNES.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mesen.mesen_overclock.Help
data.value: Use this to overclock or underclock the CPU. NOTE: Overclocking can cause issues in some games.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mesen.mesen_overclock_type.Help
data.value: Increases the number of scanlines in the PPU, before or after the NMI signal is triggered at the end of the visible frame. This effectively gives more time for games to perform calculations, which can reduce slowdowns in games. 'Before NMI' is the preferred option for overclocking, 'After NMI' should only be used if it does not work as expected.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mesen.mesen_region.Help
data.value: When set to Auto, the emulator will try to detect the game's region (NTSC or PAL), however this is not always possible. When there is nothing to suggest a game is for the PAL region, the NTSC region will be used by default. Dendy is used to mimic a number of different NES clones, in particular, the Dendy, which was a popular clone in Russia.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mesen.mesen_ramstate.Help
data.value: On a console, the RAM's state at power on is undetermined and relatively random. This option lets you select Mesen's behavior when initializing RAM: set all bits to 0, set all bits to 1, or randomize the value of each bit.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mesen.mesen_fdsautoinsertdisk.Help
data.value: By default, the FDS boots with no disk inserted in the drive. This option makes it so the player does not need to manually insert disk 1, side A manually.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mesen.mesen_fdsfastforwardload.Help
data.value: FDS games contain a large number of load screens due to their data being stored on floppy drives. Mesen needs to emulate this floppy drive's speed to ensure accurate emulation. This option makes it so Mesen runs the emulation as fast as it can when a game is loading data from the disk, which greatly reduces the time spent on loading screens.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mesen.mesen_ntsc_filter.Help
data.value: Select a filter to apply to the picture. Blargg filters are fast, Bisqwit filters are slower.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mesen.mesen_nospritelimit.Help
data.value: The NES can normally only draw up to 8 sprites per line, this limitation is indirectly responsible for some of the flickering seen in games at times. When this option is enabled, the limit is disabled, allowing up to 64 sprites to be drawn on the same line.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mesen.mesen_overscan_left.Help
data.value: This overscan setting allow you to cut out pixels on the left side of the screen.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mesen.mesen_overscan_right.Help
data.value: This overscan setting allow you to cut out pixels on the right side of the screen.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mesen.mesen_overscan_up.Help
data.value: This overscan setting allow you to cut out pixels on the top of the screen.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mesen.mesen_overscan_down.Help
data.value: This overscan setting allow you to cut out pixels on the bottom of the screen.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mesen.mesen_screenrotation.Help
data.value: Rotates the display by the specified angle. This is useful to play games (generally homebrew games) designed for a vertical display.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mesen.mesen_mute_triangle_ultrasonic.Help
data.value: This option mutes the triangle channel under certain conditions, which prevents it from causing popping sounds.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mesen.mesen_reduce_dmc_popping.Help
data.value: This option prevents games from changing the output of the DMC channel too abruptly, which often causes popping sounds.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mesen.mesen_swap_duty_cycle.Help
data.value: This option is to mimic some older NES clones that had incorrect sound output for both of the square channels. It greatly alters the sound in some games, and shouldn't be enabled unless you want this behavior.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mesen.mesen_disable_noise_mode_flag.Help
data.value: Very early Famicom models did not implement this feature, so this option is available to mimic early Famicom consoles. It changes the sound output of the noise channel in some games, and shouldn't be enabled unless you want this behavior.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mesen.mesen_controllerturbospeed.Help
data.value: Configure the controller turbo buttons speed.

data.name: Emulation.Emulator.mesen2.Description
data.value: Emulates compatible Nintendo systems with Mesen2.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mesen2.mesen_fdsautoinsertdisk.Help
data.value: Automatically insert disks on FDS games

data.name: Emulation.Option.mesen2.mesen_fdsfastforwardload
data.value: System - FDS Fast Forward On Load

data.name: Emulation.Option.mesen2.mesen_fdsfastforwardload.Help
data.value: Fast forward while FDS is loading

data.name: Emulation.Option.mesen2.mesen_snes_high_res_blend_mode.Help
data.value: Select the SNES high-resolution blend mode

data.name: Emulation.Option.mesen2.mesen_gameboy_model.Help
data.value: Select the Game Boy model to emulate

data.name: Emulation.Option.mesen2.mesen_gameboy_blend_frames.Help
data.value: Blend Game Boy frames for a smoother image

data.name: Emulation.Option.mesen2.mesen_gameboy_remove_sprite_limit
data.value: Enhancements - Game Boy Remove Sprite Limit

data.name: Emulation.Option.mesen2.mesen_gameboy_remove_sprite_limit.Help
data.value: Remove the Game Boy sprite limit

data.name: Emulation.Option.mesen2.mesen_gameboy_hide_sgb_borders
data.value: Video - Game Boy Hide SGB Borders

data.name: Emulation.Option.mesen2.mesen_disable_game_genie_bus_conflicts
data.value: Enhancements - Disable Game Genie Bus Conflicts

data.name: Emulation.Emulator.nestopia.Description
data.value: Emulates compatible Nintendo systems with Nestopia.

data.name: Emulation.Option.nestopia.nestopia_favored_system.Help
data.value: System to prefer for images that do not say which one they want. Images that do say, and images found in the NstDatabase.xml database file, are unaffected. Only applies while 'Force System' is set to 'Auto'. Requires a restart.

data.name: Emulation.Option.nestopia.nestopia_force_system.Help
data.value: Ignore the system the image asks for and use this one instead. Changing this setting will restart the game.

data.name: Emulation.Option.nestopia.nestopia_fds_auto_insert.Help
data.value: Automatically insert first FDS disk on reset.

data.name: Emulation.Option.nestopia.nestopia_fds_savefile_format.Help
data.value: Define which format will be used by savefiles generated for FDS games. Based on the format chosen, FDS savefiles might be used interchangeably with other cores and standalone emulators. It is recommended to use with caution, as improper handling may cause undesired overwrites, or deletion of the existing saves.

data.name: Emulation.Option.nestopia.nestopia_palette.Help
data.value: Color palette to be used. If 'Custom' is selected, the palette used will be taken from the 'custom.pal' file placed in the RetroArch System/BIOS directory.

data.name: Emulation.Option.nestopia.nestopia_overscan_v_top.Help
data.value: Mask out (vertically) the potentially random glitchy video output that would have been hidden by the bezel around the edge of a standard-definition television screen.

data.name: Emulation.Option.nestopia.nestopia_overscan_v_bottom.Help
data.value: Mask out (vertically) the potentially random glitchy video output that would have been hidden by the bezel around the edge of a standard-definition television screen.

data.name: Emulation.Option.nestopia.nestopia_overscan_h_left.Help
data.value: Mask out (horizontally) the potentially random glitchy video output that would have been hidden by the bezel around the edge of a standard-definition television screen.

data.name: Emulation.Option.nestopia.nestopia_overscan_h_right.Help
data.value: Mask out (horizontally) the potentially random glitchy video output that would have been hidden by the bezel around the edge of a standard-definition television screen.

data.name: Emulation.Option.nestopia.nestopia_aspect.Help
data.value: RetroArch's aspect ratio must be set to 'Core Provided' in the Video settings. 'Auto' will use the NstDatabase.xml database file for region autodetection, defaulting to NTSC if there is no database present. 'Auto', 'NTSC' and 'PAL' give the picture its correct pixel aspect ratio, so it narrows as the overscan mask is raised. '4:3' and '5:4' are display aspect ratios, and fill that shape whatever is masked. 'Uncorrected' gives square pixels.

data.name: Emulation.Option.nestopia.nestopia_audio_filter.Help
data.value: Approximate the analog stage that follows the DAC on real hardware, by applying a first order 220Hz high pass and a first order 14kHz low pass to the mixed output. This removes the DC offset the mixer sits on and rolls off the extreme treble.

data.name: Emulation.Option.nestopia.nestopia_show_advanced_av_settings.Help
data.value: Enable configuration of low-level audio channel parameters.

data.name: Emulation.Option.nestopia.nestopia_select_adapter.Help
data.value: Manually select a 4 Player Adapter if needed. Some games will not recognize the adapter correctly through the NstDatabase.xml database, this option should help fix that.

data.name: Emulation.Option.nestopia.nestopia_arkanoid_device.Help
data.value: Select the device you wish to use for the Arkanoid paddle.

data.name: Emulation.Option.nestopia.nestopia_arkanoid_paddle_range.Help
data.value: Set the range for the Arkanoid paddle.

data.name: Emulation.Option.nestopia.nestopia_zapper_device.Help
data.value: Select the device you wish to use for the Zapper.

data.name: Emulation.Option.nestopia.nestopia_show_crosshair.Help
data.value: Set whether to show the crosshair when the Zapper is used.

data.name: Emulation.Option.nestopia.nestopia_turbo_pulse.Help
data.value: Set the turbo pulse speed for the Turbo B and Turbo A buttons.

data.name: Emulation.Option.nestopia.nestopia_dmc_pop_reducer.Help
data.value: Halve large direct writes to the DMC level, which are otherwise heard as clicks. Inaccurate, and quietens samples streamed through $4011 as large swings.

data.name: Emulation.Option.nestopia.nestopia_genie_distortion.Help
data.value: The Game Genie cheat device could inadvertently introduce sound distortion in games. By enabling this, you can simulate the distortion it would add to a game's sound.

data.name: Emulation.Option.nestopia.nestopia_ram_power_state.Help
data.value: RAM values on power up. Some games rely on initial RAM values for random number generation as an example.

data.name: Emulation.Emulator.quicknes.Description
data.value: Emulates compatible Nintendo systems with QuickNES.

data.name: Emulation.Option.quicknes.quicknes_aspect_ratio_par.Help
data.value: This will only apply when RetroArch's aspect ratio is set to 'Core provided' in the Video settings.

data.name: Emulation.Option.quicknes.quicknes_use_overscan_h.Help
data.value: Disable this to crop out (horizontally) the potentially random glitchy video output that would have been hidden by the bezel around the edge of a standard-definition television screen.

data.name: Emulation.Option.quicknes.quicknes_use_overscan_v.Help
data.value: Disable this to crop out (vertically) the potentially random glitchy video output that would have been hidden by the bezel around the edge of a standard-definition television screen.

data.name: Emulation.Option.quicknes.quicknes_palette.Help
data.value: Specifies which color palette to use when decoding the NTSC video signal output by the NES.

data.name: Emulation.Option.quicknes.quicknes_no_sprite_limit.Help
data.value: Removes the 8-sprite-per-scanline hardware limit. This reduces flickering but can cause visual glitches, as some games exploit the hardware limit to generate special effects.

data.name: Emulation.Option.quicknes.quicknes_audio_samplerate.Help
data.value: The NES has no sample-based audio hardware; sound is synthesized in realtime, so there is no fixed output samplerate. Select the rate the core renders audio at. Higher rates reduce aliasing in expansion-chip audio (VRC6, VRC7, Namco 163) and cut low-pass 'smearing' from frontend resampling, at a small performance cost. 'Auto' picks whichever supported rate is closest to the frontend's target output rate. Output rate does not affect savestates or netplay.

data.name: Emulation.Option.quicknes.quicknes_audio_nonlinear.Help
data.value: Configure audio emulation. 'Non-Linear' simulates the non-linear channel mixing of the NES APU. 'Linear' uses a less accurate approximation, which reduces quality but increases performance on low-end hardware. 'Stereo Panning' adds depth to the NES mono output through the use of panning techniques and reverb effects.

data.name: Emulation.Option.quicknes.quicknes_audio_eq.Help
data.value: Adjust the balance between audio frequency components with a custom equalizer preset.

data.name: Emulation.Option.quicknes.quicknes_turbo_enable.Help
data.value: Enables the use of the Turbo A and Turbo B buttons.

data.name: Emulation.Option.quicknes.quicknes_turbo_pulse_width.Help
data.value: Specifies both the width and spacing (in frames) of input 'pulses' when the Turbo A and Turbo B buttons are held down. For example, the default setting of '3' corresponds to a (60/(3+3)) = 10 Hz turbo frequency (10 presses per second).

data.name: Emulation.Option.quicknes.quicknes_up_down_allowed.Help
data.value: Enabling this will allow pressing / quickly alternating / holding both left and right (or up and down) directions at the same time. This may cause movement-based glitches.

data.name: Emulation.Emulator.rustynes.Description
data.value: Emulates compatible Nintendo systems with RustyNES.

data.name: Emulation.Emulator.doublecherrygb.Description
data.value: Emulates compatible Nintendo systems with DoubleCherryGB.

data.name: Emulation.Option.doublecherrygb.dcgb_gbc_detect_as_GBA
data.value: Detect as Played on Game Boy Advance

data.name: Emulation.Option.doublecherrygb.dcgb_gbc_detect_as_GBA.Help
data.value:
Some Game Boy Color games offer enhanced features when played on a Game Boy Advance.
Known GBA-enhanced games: - Shantae - Wendy: Every Witch Way - Zelda: Oracle of Ages / Seasons - Medarot 5 - Mega Man Extreme 2

data.name: Emulation.Option.doublecherrygb.dcgb_rtc_use_system_clock.Help
data.value: Controls how the in-game Real-Time Clock (RTC) ticks. 'Real-Time' uses your host device's system clock (resists fast-forwarding; time passes while the emulator is closed). 'Emulated' calculates time strictly based on emulated CPU cycles.

data.name: Emulation.Option.doublecherrygb.dcgb_gb_lcd_ghosting.Help
data.value: Simulates the screen ghosting/motion blur effect of the original Game Boy (DMG) DotMatrix LCD.

data.name: Emulation.Option.doublecherrygb.dcgb_gb_dotmatrix_upscale.Help
data.value: Simulates the physical DotMatrix pixel grid of the original Game Boy. Intended for hardware without GPU or shader support. If your device supports them, use shaders instead.

data.name: Emulation.Option.doublecherrygb.dcgb_gb_default_palette.Help
data.value: Selects the default color palette for original Game Boy games. You can cycle through palettes during gameplay by pressing L1/LB and R1/RB.

data.name: Emulation.Option.doublecherrygb.dcgb_gb_use_gbc_lcd
data.value: Use Game Boy Color LCD Options

data.name: Emulation.Option.doublecherrygb.dcgb_gb_use_gbc_lcd.Help
data.value: Forces the core to use the Game Boy Color LCD layout and settings instead of the standard original Game Boy DotMatrix grid.

data.name: Emulation.Option.doublecherrygb.dcgb_gbc_lcdcolor_correction.Help
data.value: Simulates the screen saturation of the physical GBC display. Disable this option if you are using external RetroArch shaders, as most shaders already apply color correction.

data.name: Emulation.Option.doublecherrygb.dcgb_gbc_lcd_interlacing.Help
data.value: Simulates the interlacing scanline effect of the Game Boy Color LCD to add visual depth.

data.name: Emulation.Option.doublecherrygb.dcgb_gbc_lcd_interlacing_brightnesss.Help
data.value: Adjusts the intensity of the interlacing effect. Keep this value low when not using shaders. Higher values are recommended when combined with a shader to make the effect visible.

data.name: Emulation.Option.doublecherrygb.dcgb_gbc_RGB_SubPixel_Simulation
data.value: GBC LCD RGB Subpixel Scale Factor

data.name: Emulation.Option.doublecherrygb.dcgb_gbc_RGB_SubPixel_Simulation.Help
data.value:
Simulates physical GBC subpixels by upscaling and replacing each color pixel with corresponding RGB components.
For best results: - Enable 'Integer Scaling' in RetroArch (Settings -> Video -> Scaling). - A core restart may be required after changing this setting.

data.name: Emulation.Option.doublecherrygb.dcgb_gbc_LCD_blur.Help
data.value: Applies a display blur effect. This setting is highly CPU-intensive. Turn it off on weaker hardware or utilize shaders instead.

data.name: Emulation.Option.doublecherrygb.dcgb_light_temperature.Help
data.value: Simulates an ambient light source reflecting off non-backlit Game Boy screens by adjusting the color temperature. This option has no effect when emulating an original Game Boy (DMG) model.

data.name: Emulation.Option.doublecherrygb.dcgb_audio_filter.Help
data.value: Enables an experimental low-pass/audio smoothing filter.

data.name: Emulation.Option.doublecherrygb.dcgb_input_polling_rate.Help
data.value: Increases the input polling rate for improved controller responsiveness. While it reduces latency in most games, it may feel overly sensitive in others.

data.name: Emulation.Option.doublecherrygb.dcgb_singleplayer_linked_devive.Help
data.value: Keeps the link cable device on 'Auto' detection unless you need to manually force a specific hardware expansion for unsupported software.

data.name: Emulation.Option.doublecherrygb.dcgb_gb_printer_png_upscale.Help
data.value: Sets the target paper size format for the exported Game Boy Printer image outputs.

data.name: Emulation.Option.doublecherrygb.dcgb_gb_printer_png_alignment.Help
data.value: Determines the canvas alignment for saved Game Boy Printer images.

data.name: Emulation.Option.doublecherrygb.dcgb_pkmbuddyboy_auto_mew.Help
data.value: Automatically trades a Mew or Celebi in the cable club if you do not currently own one.

data.name: Emulation.Option.doublecherrygb.dcgb_pkmbuddyboy_weekly_dtistributions events.Help
data.value: Enables weekly offline simulated Pokémon distribution events via the PKMBuddy Boy.

data.name: Emulation.Option.doublecherrygb.dcgb_power_antenna_use_rumble.Help
data.value: Emulates the unique hardware add-ons packaged with 'Keitai Denjuu Telefang' and 'Network Adventure Bugsite'. DoubleCherryGB replicates this functionality via the RetroArch LED API and adds rumble support.

data.name: Emulation.Option.doublecherrygb.dcgb_alleyway_analog_enabled.Help
data.value: Selects the input method used to control the Alleyway Link Cable Controller.

data.name: Emulation.Option.doublecherrygb.dcgb_infrared_lockstep.Help
data.value: Forces synchronized step-by-step execution across core instances. Needed for precise GBC Infrared (IR) features like Card Pop!. Note: Infrared emulation is experimental.

data.name: Emulation.Option.doublecherrygb.dcgb_infrared_tv_remote_auto_signal.Help
data.value: Certain GBC games unlock secrets via household IR TV remotes. While the keyboard Numpad can be used to send manual codes, this option transmits randomized signals automatically.

data.name: Emulation.Option.doublecherrygb.dcgb_emulated_gameboys.Help
data.value: Defines the fixed number of concurrent emulated instances (1-16). Alternatively, players can hot-join at any time during gameplay by pressing the LB/L1 button on their controller.

data.name: Emulation.Option.doublecherrygb.dcgb_netplay_mode.Help
data.value: Keep on 'Auto' unless you need to force a fallback protocol for stubborn or officially unsupported multiplayer software.

data.name: Emulation.Option.doublecherrygb.dcgb_multiplayer_linked_devive.Help
data.value: Selects the multi-device link topology. Keep on 'Auto' unless manual override is required for specific rom hacks or multiplayer games.

data.name: Emulation.Option.doublecherrygb.dcgb_screen_placement.Help
data.value: Sets the screen arrangement strategy for local multiplayer sessions.

data.name: Emulation.Option.doublecherrygb.dcgb_single_screen_mp.Help
data.value: Configures visibility parameters for remote network players' video streams.

data.name: Emulation.Option.doublecherrygb.dcgb_audio_output.Help
data.value: Selects which emulated Game Boy instance outputs its sound to the host system audio.

data.name: Emulation.Option.doublecherrygb.dcgb_cocktailtable_mode.Help
data.value: Rotates screen configurations dynamically for usage in custom physical head-to-head Arcade Cocktail Cabinets (Strictly limited to 2-Player setups).

data.name: Emulation.Option.doublecherrygb.dcgb_mobile_adatper_enabled.Help
data.value:
Enables emulation of the Japanese Mobile Adapter GB peripheral.
Supported Titles: - Pokemon Crystal (Japan or mobile adapter patched) - Game Boy Wars 3 - Hello Kitty Happy House - Mobile Golf - Mobile Trainer - Net de Get

data.name: Emulation.Option.doublecherrygb.dcgb_mobile_adapter_show_p2p_phonenumber
data.value: Show your Phone Number at start

data.name: Emulation.Option.doublecherrygb.dcgb_mobile_adapter_show_p2p_phonenumber.Help
data.value:
Shows your P2P phone number at startup.
Warning: Without a relay server, this exposes your public IP address. Only share this with trusted users.

data.name: Emulation.Option.doublecherrygb.dcgb_mobile_adatper_device_color.Help
data.value: Sets the cosmetic shell color of the emulated Mobile Adapter device.

data.name: Emulation.Option.doublecherrygb.dcgb_mobile_adatper_dns_ip.Help
data.value:
Official Nintendo servers are offline. You can host infrastructure replacements yourself, using custom stacks like REON: https://github.com/REONTeam/reon.
For custom configuration edit the mobile_adapter_gb_custom_server_config.ini in your retroarch systems folder.

data.name: Emulation.Option.doublecherrygb.dcgb_mobile_adatper_dns_port.Help
data.value:
Specify the target port connection for the custom network infrastructure.
For custom configuration edit the mobile_adapter_gb_custom_server_config.ini in your retroarch systems folder.

data.name: Emulation.Option.doublecherrygb.dcgb_mobile_adatper_use_relay_server.Help
data.value:
Use a custom relay server for P2P Calls.
For custom configuration edit the mobile_adapter_gb_custom_server_config.ini in your retroarch systems folder.

data.name: Emulation.Option.doublecherrygb.dcgb_mobile_adatper_relay_ip.Help
data.value:
Specify the target port connection for the custom network infrastructure.
For custom configuration edit the mobile_adapter_gb_custom_server_config.ini in your retroarch systems folder.

data.name: Emulation.Option.doublecherrygb.dcgb_mobile_adatper_relay_port.Help
data.value:
Specify the target port connection for the custom P2P relay serber.
For custom configuration edit the mobile_adapter_gb_custom_server_config.ini in your retroarch systems folder.

data.name: Emulation.Option.doublecherrygb.dcgb_dev_log_linkcable_to_file
data.value: Log Link Cable Transfers to File

data.name: Emulation.Option.doublecherrygb.dcgb_dev_log_linkcable_to_file.Help
data.value: Dumps raw communication traffic data into files. Keep disabled unless actively reverse-engineering hexadecimal protocols, as heavy file I/O operations will bottleneck emulation speeds.

data.name: Emulation.Emulator.fixgb.Description
data.value: Emulates compatible Nintendo systems with fixGB.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gambatte.gambatte_gb_colorization.Help
data.value: Enables colorization of Game Boy games. 'Auto' selects the 'best' (most colorful/appropriate) palette. 'GBC' selects game-specific Game Boy Color palette if defined, otherwise 'GBC - Dark Green'. 'SGB' selects game-specific Super Game Boy palette if defined, otherwise 'SGB - 1A'. 'Internal' uses 'Internal Palette' core option. 'Custom' loads user-created palette from system directory.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gambatte.gambatte_gb_internal_palette.Help
data.value: Selects palette used for colorizing Game Boy games when 'GB Colorization' is set to 'Internal', or when 'GB Colorization' is set to 'Auto' and game has no pre-defined SGB/GBC palette. 'GB' palettes mimic the display of original Game Boy hardware. 'GBC' palettes are identical to the built-in presets of the Game Boy Color. 'SGB' palettes are identical to the built-in presets of the Super Game Boy.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gambatte.gambatte_gb_palette_twb64_1.Help
data.value: Selects internal colorization palette when 'Internal Palette' is set to 'TWB64 - Pack 1'.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gambatte.gambatte_gb_palette_twb64_2.Help
data.value: Selects internal colorization palette when 'Internal Palette' is set to 'TWB64 - Pack 2'.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gambatte.gambatte_gb_palette_twb64_3.Help
data.value: Selects internal colorization palette when 'Internal Palette' is set to 'TWB64 - Pack 3'.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gambatte.gambatte_gb_palette_pixelshift_1.Help
data.value: Selects internal colorization palette when 'Internal Palette' is set to 'PixelShift - Pack 1'.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gambatte.gambatte_gbc_color_correction.Help
data.value: Adjusts output colors to match the display of real Game Boy Color hardware. 'GBC Only' ensures that correction will only be applied when playing Game Boy Color games, or when using a Game Boy Color palette to colorize a Game Boy game. 'Always' applies color correction to all content, and will produce unexpected/suboptimal results when using 'GB' or 'SGB' internal color palettes.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gambatte.gambatte_gbc_color_correction_mode.Help
data.value: Specifies method used when performing color correction. 'Accurate' produces output almost indistinguishable from a real Game Boy Color LCD panel. 'Fast' merely darkens colors and reduces saturation, and may be used on low-end hardware if the 'Accurate' method is too slow.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gambatte.gambatte_gbc_frontlight_position.Help
data.value: Simulates the physical response of the Game Boy Color LCD panel when illuminated from different angles. 'Central' represents standard color reproduction. 'Above Screen' increases brightness. 'Below Screen' reduces brightness. This setting only applies when 'Color Correction Mode' is set to 'Accurate'.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gambatte.gambatte_dark_filter_level.Help
data.value: Enable luminosity-based brightness reduction. May be used to avoid glare/eye strain when playing games with white backgrounds, which are intended for display on a non-backlit Game Boy Color and can therefore appear uncomfortably bright when viewed on a modern backlit screen.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gambatte.gambatte_mix_frames.Help
data.value: Simulates LCD ghosting effects. 'Simple' performs a 50:50 mix of the current and previous frames. 'LCD Ghosting' mimics natural LCD response times by combining multiple buffered frames. 'Simple' blending is required when playing games that rely on LCD ghosting for transparency effects (Wave Race, Ballistic, Chikyuu Kaihou Gun ZAS...).

data.name: Emulation.Option.gambatte.gambatte_audio_resampler.Help
data.value: Specify which algorithm to use when resampling generated audio (the Game Boy audio rate is limited only by its CPU write speed, such that 'native' frequencies are impractical on modern sound devices and must be downsampled). 'Sinc' produces the highest quality. 'Cosine' improves performance on low-end hardware.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gambatte.gambatte_gb_hwmode.Help
data.value: Specify which type of hardware to emulate. 'Auto' is recommended. Selecting 'GBA' unlocks extra features in certain 'GBA Enhanced' Game Boy Color games (Shantae, Wendy - Every Witch Way, Legend of Zelda: Oracle of Seasons/Ages...).

data.name: Emulation.Option.gambatte.gambatte_gb_bootloader.Help
data.value: Enable support for official Game Boy and Game Boy Color bootloaders, with corresponding start-up logo animations.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gambatte.gambatte_up_down_allowed.Help
data.value: Enabling this will allow pressing/quickly alternating/holding both left and right (or up and down) directions at the same time. This may cause movement-based glitches.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gambatte.gambatte_turbo_period.Help
data.value: Specify the repeat interval (in frames) when holding down the Turbo A/B buttons.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gambatte.gambatte_rumble_level.Help
data.value: Enables haptic feedback effects for supported games (Pokemon Pinball, Perfect Dark...).

data.name: Emulation.Option.gambatte.gambatte_show_gb_link_settings.Help
data.value: Enable configuration of networked Game Link (multiplayer) options. NOTE: Quick Menu may need to be toggled for this setting to take effect.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gambatte.gambatte_gb_link_mode.Help
data.value: When enabling networked Game Link functionality, specify whether current instance should run as a server or client.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gambatte.gambatte_gb_link_network_port.Help
data.value: Specify port used for Game Link network communication.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gearboy.gearboy_model.Help
data.value: Select which hardware model is emulated. 'Auto' automatically selects the best model based on the loaded ROM header. 'Game Boy DMG' forces original Game Boy hardware. 'Game Boy Advance' forces Game Boy Advance mode, which enables minor hardware differences present when running Game Boy games on a GBA.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gearboy.gearboy_mapper.Help
data.value: Select which Memory Bank Controller (MBC or mapper) is emulated. 'Auto' automatically selects the best MBC based on the ROM header. Use manual selection only if a game has issues with automatic detection.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gearboy.gearboy_sgb.Help
data.value: When enabled, compatible ROMs will run in Super Game Boy mode. When disabled, SGB-compatible ROMs will run as standard Game Boy (DMG) games.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gearboy.gearboy_sgb_border.Help
data.value: When enabled, the Super Game Boy border is displayed around the game screen (256x224). When disabled, only the game screen is shown (160x144).

data.name: Emulation.Option.gearboy.gearboy_bootrom_dmg.Help
data.value: Enable or disable the original Game Boy (DMG) bootrom. When enabled, the bootrom will execute on startup just like on real hardware, showing the Nintendo logo scroll animation. The 'dmg_boot.bin' file must be present in RetroArch's system directory.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gearboy.gearboy_bootrom_gbc.Help
data.value: Enable or disable the Game Boy Color bootrom. When enabled, the bootrom will execute on startup just like on real hardware, showing the Game Boy Color boot animation. The 'cgb_boot.bin' file must be present in RetroArch's system directory.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gearboy.gearboy_palette.Help
data.value: Select a color palette for original Game Boy (DMG) games. This setting has no effect on Game Boy Color games, which use their own built-in color palettes.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gearboy.gearboy_color_correction.Help
data.value: Apply color correction for Game Boy Color games to simulate the original GBC LCD screen output. When disabled, raw RGB colors are displayed which may appear overly saturated on modern displays.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gearboy.gearboy_no_sprite_limit.Help
data.value: Remove the per-line sprite limit. This reduces flickering but may cause glitches in certain games. It's best to keep this option disabled.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gearboy.gearboy_tilt_source.Help
data.value: Select the input source for tilt control in MBC7 games (e.g. Kirby Tilt 'n' Tumble). 'Mouse' uses relative mouse movement. 'Sensor' uses the device's real accelerometer. 'Analog Stick' uses the left analog stick for tilt (D-Pad used for directions).

data.name: Emulation.Option.gearboy.gearboy_sensor_sensitivity_x.Help
data.value: Set the horizontal sensor sensitivity for tilt control in MBC7 games.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gearboy.gearboy_sensor_sensitivity_y.Help
data.value: Set the vertical sensor sensitivity for tilt control in MBC7 games.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gearboy.gearboy_sensor_invert_x.Help
data.value: Invert horizontal sensor axis for tilt control.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gearboy.gearboy_sensor_invert_y.Help
data.value: Invert vertical sensor axis for tilt control.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gearboy.gearboy_mouse_sensitivity_x.Help
data.value: Set the horizontal mouse sensitivity for tilt control in MBC7 games.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gearboy.gearboy_mouse_sensitivity_y.Help
data.value: Set the vertical mouse sensitivity for tilt control in MBC7 games.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gearboy.gearboy_mouse_invert_x.Help
data.value: Invert horizontal mouse axis for tilt control.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gearboy.gearboy_mouse_invert_y.Help
data.value: Invert vertical mouse axis for tilt control.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gearboy.gearboy_analog_sensitivity_x.Help
data.value: Set the horizontal analog stick sensitivity for tilt control in MBC7 games.
