data.value: Emulates compatible Nintendo systems with gpSP.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gpsp.gpsp_bios.Help
data.value: Choose the BIOS image to use. The official BIOS must be provided by the user. Using a non-official (or builtin) BIOS might result in incompatibility problems with some games. Best results are to be achieved with the official Nintendo BIOS.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gpsp.gpsp_boot_mode.Help
data.value: Choose whether to boot the BIOS before the game or not. There's not much difference in either modes.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gpsp.gpsp_drc.Help
data.value: Dynamically recompile CPU instructions to native instructions. Greatly improves performance, but may reduce accuracy.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gpsp.gpsp_sprlim.Help
data.value: Removes the original sprite-per-scanline hardware limit. Some games might rely on the hardware limit for proper rendering (ie. hiding some sprites).

data.name: Emulation.Option.gpsp.gpsp_rtc.Help
data.value: Sets the RTC support for the emulated cartridge. Autodetect uses a ROM database that works with most commercial titles. You might need to force RTC when using homebrew or ROM hacks.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gpsp.gpsp_rtc_time_source.Help
data.value: Selects the clock used by RTC-enabled cartridges. Deterministic advances with emulated frames and is preserved in save states. System Clock follows the host clock, including time elapsed while content is not running.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gpsp.gpsp_serial.Help
data.value: Configures the serial (Link Cable) connection. Automatic will pick up a reasonable support for most known games.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gpsp.gpsp_rumble.Help
data.value: Sets the Rumble support for the emulated cartridge. Autodetect uses a ROM database that works with most commercial titles. You might want to force Rumble when using homebrew or ROM hacks that support it. You can also force-disable it if you don't like it.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gpsp.gpsp_sound_rate.Help
data.value: Internal audio rendering rate. Both values keep audio timing exact. 65536 renders the full mixer bandwidth; 32768 matches the bandwidth of real hardware's default PWM output and halves audio mixing work.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gpsp.gpsp_frameskip.Help
data.value: Skip frames to avoid audio buffer under-run (crackling). Improves performance at the expense of visual smoothness. 'Auto' skips frames when advised by the frontend. 'Auto (Threshold)' utilises the 'Frameskip Threshold (%)' setting. 'Fixed Interval' utilises the 'Frameskip Interval' setting.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gpsp.gpsp_frameskip_threshold.Help
data.value: When 'Frameskip' is set to 'Auto (Threshold)', specifies the audio buffer occupancy threshold (percentage) below which frames will be skipped. Higher values reduce the risk of crackling by causing frames to be dropped more frequently.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gpsp.gpsp_frameskip_interval.Help
data.value: When 'Frameskip' is set to 'Fixed Interval', the value set here is the number of frames omitted after a frame is rendered - i.e. '0' = 60fps, '1' = 30fps, '2' = 15fps, etc.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gpsp.gpsp_color_correction.Help
data.value: Adjusts output colors to match the display of real GBA hardware.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gpsp.gpsp_frame_mixing.Help
data.value: Simulates LCD ghosting effects by performing a 50:50 mix of the current and previous frames. Required for correct operation when playing games that exploit LCD ghosting for transparency effects (F-Zero, the Boktai series, etc.).

data.name: Emulation.Option.gpsp.gpsp_turbo_period.Help
data.value: Specify the repeat interval (in frames) when holding down the Turbo A/B buttons.

data.name: Emulation.Emulator.meteor.Description
data.value: Emulates compatible Nintendo systems with Meteor.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mgba.mgba_gb_model.Help
data.value: Runs loaded content with a specific Game Boy model. 'Autodetect' will select the most appropriate model for the current game.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mgba.mgba_use_bios.Help
data.value: Use official BIOS/bootloader for emulated hardware, if present in RetroArch's system directory.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mgba.mgba_skip_bios.Help
data.value: When using an official BIOS/bootloader, skip the start-up logo animation. This setting is ignored when 'Use BIOS File if Found' is disabled.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mgba.mgba_gb_colors.Help
data.value: Selects which palette is used for Game Boy games that are not Game Boy Color or Super Game Boy compatible, or if the model is forced to Game Boy.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mgba.mgba_gb_colors_preset.Help
data.value: Use the palettes for Game Boy games that have presets on the Game Boy Color or Super Game Boy.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mgba.mgba_sgb_borders.Help
data.value: Display Super Game Boy borders when running Super Game Boy enhanced games.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mgba.mgba_color_correction.Help
data.value: Adjusts output colors to match the display of real GBA/GBC hardware.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mgba.mgba_interframe_blending.Help
data.value: Simulates LCD ghosting effects. 'Simple' performs a 50:50 mix of the current and previous frames. 'Smart' attempts to detect screen flickering, and only performs a 50:50 mix on affected pixels. 'LCD Ghosting' mimics natural LCD response times by combining multiple buffered frames. 'Simple' or 'Smart' blending is required when playing games that aggressively exploit LCD ghosting for transparency effects (Wave Race, Chikyuu Kaihou Gun ZAS, F-Zero, the Boktai series...).

data.name: Emulation.Option.mgba.mgba_audio_low_pass_filter.Help
data.value: Enables a low pass audio filter to reduce the 'harshness' of generated audio.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mgba.mgba_audio_low_pass_range.Help
data.value: Specifies the cut-off frequency of the low pass audio filter. A higher value increases the perceived 'strength' of the filter, since a wider range of the high frequency spectrum is attenuated.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mgba.mgba_allow_opposing_directions.Help
data.value: Enabling this will allow pressing / quickly alternating / holding both left and right (or up and down) directions at the same time. This may cause movement-based glitches.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mgba.mgba_solar_sensor_level.Help
data.value: Sets ambient sunlight intensity. Can be used by games that included a solar sensor in their cartridges, e.g: the Boktai series.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mgba.mgba_force_gbp.Help
data.value: Enabling this will allow compatible games with the Game Boy Player boot logo to make the controller rumble. Due to how Nintendo decided this feature should work, it may cause glitches such as flickering or lag in some of these games.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mgba.mgba_idle_optimization.Help
data.value: Reduce system load by optimizing so-called 'idle-loops' - sections in the code where nothing happens, but the CPU runs at full speed (like a car revving in neutral). Improves performance, and should be enabled on low-end hardware.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mgba.mgba_frameskip.Help
data.value: Skip frames to avoid audio buffer under-run (crackling). Improves performance at the expense of visual smoothness. 'Auto' skips frames when advised by the frontend. 'Auto (Threshold)' utilises the 'Frameskip Threshold (%)' setting. 'Fixed Interval' utilises the 'Frameskip Interval' setting.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mgba.mgba_frameskip_threshold.Help
data.value: When 'Frameskip' is set to 'Auto (Threshold)', specifies the audio buffer occupancy threshold (percentage) below which frames will be skipped. Higher values reduce the risk of crackling by causing frames to be dropped more frequently.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mgba.mgba_frameskip_interval.Help
data.value: When 'Frameskip' is set to 'Fixed Interval', the value set here is the number of frames omitted after a frame is rendered - i.e. '0' = 60fps, '1' = 30fps, '2' = 15fps, etc.

data.value: Emulates compatible Nintendo systems with VBA-M.

data.name: Emulation.Option.vbam.vbam_usebios.Help
data.value: Use official BIOS when available. Core needs to be restarted for changes to apply.

data.name: Emulation.Option.vbam.vbam_forceRTCenable.Help
data.value: Forces the internal real-time clock to be enabled regardless of rom. Useable for rom patches that require clock to be enabled (e.g., Pokemon).

data.name: Emulation.Option.vbam.vbam_gbHardware.Help

data.name: Emulation.Option.vbam.vbam_allowcolorizerhack.Help
data.value: Allows Colorizer hacked GB games (e.g. DX patched games) to normally run in GBC/GBA hardware type. This also disables the use of bios file. NOT RECOMMENDED for use on non-colorized games.

data.name: Emulation.Option.vbam.vbam_palettes.Help
data.value: Set Game Boy palettes to use.

data.name: Emulation.Option.vbam.vbam_showborders.Help
data.value: When enabled, if loaded content is SGB compatible, this will show the border from the game if available.

data.name: Emulation.Option.vbam.vbam_gbcoloroption.Help
data.value: Applies color correction which fixes colors in some games.

data.name: Emulation.Option.vbam.vbam_lcdfilter.Help
data.value: Darkens the onscreen colors by applying a screen filter.

data.name: Emulation.Option.vbam.vbam_interframeblending.Help
data.value: Simulates LCD ghosting effects. 'Smart' attempts to detect screen flickering, and only performs a 50:50 mix on affected pixels, while 'Motion Blur' mimics natural LCD response times by combining multiple buffered frames. 'Smart' blending is required when playing games that aggressively exploit LCD ghosting for transparency effects (Wave Race, Chikyuu Kaihou Gun ZAS, F-Zero, the Boktai series...).

data.name: Emulation.Option.vbam.vbam_soundfiltering.Help
data.value: Sets the amount of filtering to use. Higher value reduces higher frequencies.

data.name: Emulation.Option.vbam.vbam_turboenable.Help
data.value: Enable or disable gamepad turbo buttons.

data.name: Emulation.Option.vbam.vbam_turbodelay.Help
data.value: Repeat rate of turbo triggers in frames. Higher value triggers more.

data.name: Emulation.Option.vbam.vbam_solarsensor.Help
data.value: Adjusts simulated solar level in Boktai games. L2/R2 buttons can also be used to quickly change levels.

data.name: Emulation.Option.vbam.vbam_astick_deadzone.Help
data.value: Set deadzone (in percent) of analog sticks.

data.name: Emulation.Option.vbam.vbam_gyro_sensitivity.Help
data.value: Default bind is left analog. Used to adjust sensitivity level for gyro-enabled games.

data.name: Emulation.Option.vbam.vbam_tilt_sensitivity.Help
data.value: Default bind is right analog. Used to adjust sensitivity level for gyro-enabled games.

data.name: Emulation.Option.vbam.vbam_swap_astick.Help

data.name: Emulation.Option.vbam.vbam_sound_1.Help

data.name: Emulation.Option.vbam.vbam_sound_2.Help

data.name: Emulation.Option.vbam.vbam_sound_3.Help

data.name: Emulation.Option.vbam.vbam_layer_8.Help

data.name: Emulation.Option.dolphin.dolphin_main_load_game_into_memory.Help

data.name: Emulation.Option.dolphin.dolphin_early_presentation.Help

data.name: Emulation.Option.dolphin.dolphin_dsp_hle.Help

data.name: Emulation.Option.dolphin.dolphin_gc_sp1.Help

data.name: Emulation.Option.dolphin.dolphin_enable_gamecube_mic.Help
data.value: Emulate the official GameCube microphone accessory. Restart core after changing this option.

data.name: Emulation.Option.dolphin.dolphin_hotkey_activate_microphone.Help
data.value: Button to hold or press to activate the microphone input. Selecting OFF disables microphone activation.

data.name: Emulation.Option.dolphin.dolphin_alt_gc_ports_on_wii.Help

data.name: Emulation.Option.dolphin.dolphin_bluetooth_passthrough.Help

data.name: Emulation.Option.dolphin.dolphin_crop_overscan.Help

data.name: Emulation.Option.dolphin.dolphin_disable_copy_filter.Help

data.name: Emulation.Option.dolphin.dolphin_enhance_hdr_output.Help

data.name: Emulation.Option.dolphin.dolphin_mipmap_detection.Help

data.name: Emulation.Option.dolphin.dolphin_ir_passthrough.Help

The frontend supplies up to four IR objects on pointer indices 1-4; Wiimote IR Mode, Total Yaw, Total Pitch and Vertical Offset are all bypassed. For frontends that know the real geometry (a VR room, a tracked light gun) this is exact, and it carries roll and distance, which a cursor cannot. Leave off for a mouse or a gamepad.

data.name: Emulation.Emulator.parallel_n64.Description
data.value: Emulates compatible Nintendo systems with ParaLLEl N64.

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-upscaling.Help
data.value: Render at a multiple of the console's resolution. ParaLLEl-RDP honours every factor; Angrylion renders at up to 4x and treats 8x as 4x.

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-parallel-rdp-native-texture-lod
data.value: Use native texture LOD when upscaling

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-parallel-rdp-native-texture-lod.Help
data.value: Pick texture mip levels as the console would, from a console pixel's footprint rather than an upscaled pixel's. Without it an upscaled render selects sharper levels, and games that use the level as a switch show the wrong image (the painting at the end of the castle corridor in Super Mario 64). Honoured by ParaLLEl-RDP and Angrylion.

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-aleck64-testmode.Help
data.value: Boot the arcade board's test menu instead of the game.

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-aleck64-coinage.Help
data.value: Coins needed per credit (Star Soldier, Vivid Dolls, Hi Pai Paradise 1/2).

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-aleck64-difficulty.Help
data.value: Game difficulty (Star Soldier, Vivid Dolls, Hi Pai Paradise 1/2).

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-aleck64-demosound.Help
data.value: Play sound in attract mode (Star Soldier, Hi Pai Paradise 1/2).

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-aleck64-language.Help
data.value: In-game language for Star Soldier: Vanishing Earth.

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-aleck64-players.Help
data.value: Number of players supported by the cabinet.

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-mouse-mode.Help
data.value: Use mouse input to control the N64 analog stick with player 1. The mouse takes over whenever the real stick is neutral. Useful for FPS games.

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-mouse-sensitivity-x.Help
data.value: Horizontal mouse sensitivity. Negative values invert the axis. Set to 0 to disable horizontal movement.

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-mouse-sensitivity-y.Help
data.value: Vertical mouse sensitivity. Negative values invert the axis; the default is negative because positive mouse Y points down. Set to 0 for Doom-like horizontal-only control.

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-mouse-left.Help
data.value: Map mouse left click to an N64 button.

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-mouse-right.Help
data.value: Map mouse right click to an N64 button.

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-mouse-middle.Help
data.value: Map mouse middle click to an N64 button.

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-mouse-wheel-up.Help
data.value: Map mouse wheel up to an N64 button.

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-mouse-wheel-down.Help
data.value: Map mouse wheel down to an N64 button.

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-astick-snap-angle-active.Help
data.value: Snap analog stick angle to multiples of 45 degrees, to better support circular design controllers that should behave like classic N64 controllers.

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-astick-snap-max-angle.Help
data.value: Maximum deviation from a 45-degree multiple at which snapping is applied (e.g. value of 5 means 85 to 95 degrees are snapped to 90).

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-astick-snap-min-displacement-percent.Help
data.value: Percentage of stick displacement from the center required before snapping activates (0 means always).

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-disable_expmem.Help
data.value: Give the console 8MB of RAM instead of 4MB, as the Expansion Pak does. Games that require the Pak (Donkey Kong 64, Majora's Mask) will not boot with this disabled. Applied when content starts.

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-parallel-rdp-synchronous.Help
data.value: Make the CPU wait for the GPU to finish rendering at RDP full sync. Disabling can improve performance but breaks games that read rendered frames back from memory (e.g. Resident Evil 2 never starts its intro FMV); such games force this on automatically.

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-send_allist_to_hle_rsp.Help
data.value: Which RSP runs the audio microcode, independently of the one running graphics. 'Same as RSP Plugin' follows the RSP Plugin setting. 'Fast (HLE)' emulates audio lists at a high level instead of cycle-by-cycle, which is faster but glitches in some games. 'Accurate (LLE)' keeps audio cycle-accurate even when graphics run on the HLE RSP, which is the pairing to use if you want HLE speed for graphics without HLE audio glitches.

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-enhanced-hle-audio.Help
data.value: Replace the audio microcode's four-tap voice interpolator with a windowed-sinc resampler. The microcode's kernel cannot band-limit a sample that is played back faster than it was recorded, so its image folds back into the audible range - the grain and grit on high-pitched sounds. This removes most of that and is slightly less muffled besides. Only affects the HLE RSP audio path. Deliberately not bit-accurate to the hardware, so leave it off if you want the exact output the console produced.

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-enhanced-hle-audio-quality.Help
data.value: How many taps the enhanced resampler uses. More taps reject more of the folded-back image and cost a little more CPU and memory: 16 taps is already a large improvement over the microcode's four, 32 and 64 taps tighten the filter further. Has no effect unless Enhanced RSP HLE Audio is enabled.

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-angrylion-deinterlace.Help
data.value: How interlaced (480i) content is displayed. 'weave' merges both fields (sharp but combs on motion), 'bob' line-doubles the current field (no combing, slight shimmer). Affects 480i games like Kuru Kuru Fever or Hanabi de Doon and hi-res title screens.

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-64dd-hardware.Help
data.value: Treat content without a recognised cartridge or disk header as a 64DD disk. Development disks and MAME/SDK dumps carry no header marker; regular cartridges and retail D64 images are identified by their header and unaffected by this setting.

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-goldeneye-tlb-hack.Help
data.value: Map GoldenEye's demand-paged 0x7F000000 code segment directly onto the ROM, bypassing the game's own TLB pager (ari64 dynarec only). Historically required for GoldenEye to run at all; on desktop-class hosts the accurate path now measures just as fast. Disable for hardware-faithful TLB behaviour or for modified ROMs that relocate the game segment, which the mapping would corrupt.

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-allow-unaligned-dma.Help
data.value: 'Allow Unaligned' causes minor issues on Taz Express; 'Force Alignment' is accurate to N64, but breaks some romhacks.

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-allow-large-roms.Help
data.value: Enable support for roms that are larger than 64 MiB.

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-gliden64-viewport-hack.Help
data.value: (GLideN64) Hack that adjusts the viewport to allow unstretched 16:9

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-gliden64-EnableNativeResFactor.Help
data.value: (GLideN64) Render at N times the native resolution.

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-gliden64-BilinearMode.Help
data.value: (GLideN64) Select a Bilinear filtering method, 3point is the original system specific way.

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-gliden64-FXAA.Help
data.value: (GLideN64) Fast Approximate Anti-Aliasing shader, moderately blur textures (0 = disabled).

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-gliden64-EnableLODEmulation.Help
data.value: (GLideN64) Calculate per-pixel Level Of Details to select texture mip levels and blend them with each other using LOD fraction.

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-gliden64-EnableFBEmulation.Help
data.value: (GLideN64) Frame/depth buffer emulation. Disabling it can shorten input lag for particular games, but also break some special effects.

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-gliden64-EnableCopyAuxToRDRAM.Help
data.value: (GLideN64) Copy auxiliary buffers to RDRAM (fixes some Game artifacts like Paper Mario Intro).

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-gliden64-EnableCopyColorToRDRAM.Help
data.value: (GLideN64) Color buffer copy to RDRAM (Off will trade compatibility for Performance).

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-gliden64-EnableCopyColorFromRDRAM.Help
data.value: (GLideN64) Always copy the color buffer from RDRAM. GLideN64 already does this by itself whenever it detects that the CPU painted the frame the VI is about to show, so this setting only adds a second, unconditional trigger for the titles that detection misses (Donkey Kong 64 anti-aliased shadows, some Indiana Jones effects). Needs Framebuffer Emulation on. Default off for the performance cost.

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-gliden64-EnableCopyDepthToRDRAM.Help
data.value: (GLideN64) Depth buffer copy to RDRAM (Off will trade compatibility for Performance).

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-gliden64-GLideN64IniBehaviour.Help
data.value: (GLideN64) When to apply GLideN64's built-in per-game settings. 'late' lets them override your choices below, 'early' lets your choices win, 'disabled' ignores them entirely.

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-gliden64-BackgroundMode.Help
data.value: (GLideN64) Render backgrounds mode (HLE only). One piece (fast), Stripped (precise).

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-gliden64-EnableHWLighting.Help
data.value: (GLideN64) Standard per-vertex lighting when disabled. Slightly different rendering.

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-gliden64-CorrectTexrectCoords.Help
data.value: (GLideN64) Make texrect coordinates continuous to avoid black lines between them.

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-gliden64-EnableInaccurateTextureCoordinates.Help
data.value: (GLideN64) Enables inaccurate texture coordinate calculations. This can improve performance and texture pack compatibity at the cost of accuracy.

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-gliden64-EnableNativeResTexrects.Help
data.value: (GLideN64) Render 2D texrects in native resolution to fix misalignment between parts of 2D image (example: Mario Kart driver selection portraits).

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-gliden64-EnableLegacyBlending.Help
data.value: (GLideN64) Do not use shaders to emulate N64 blending modes. Works faster on slow GPU. Can cause glitches.

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-gliden64-EnableFragmentDepthWrite.Help
data.value: (GLideN64) Enable writing of fragment depth. Some mobile GPUs do not support it, thus it's optional. Leave enabled.

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-gliden64-EnableN64DepthCompare.Help
data.value: (GLideN64) Enable N64 depth compare instead of OpenGL standard one. Experimental, Fast mode will have more glitches.

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-gliden64-EnableShadersStorage.Help
data.value: (GLideN64) Use persistent storage for compiled shaders.

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-gliden64-EnableTextureCache.Help
data.value: (GLideN64) Save texture cache to hard disk.

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-gliden64-EnableOverscan.Help
data.value: (GLideN64) Crop black borders from the overscan region around the screen.

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-gliden64-txEnhancementMode.Help
data.value: (GLideN64) Various Texture Filters ('As-Is' will just cache).

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-gliden64-txHiresEnable.Help
data.value: (GLideN64) Enable High-Res Texture packs if available.

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-gliden64-txHiresFullAlphaChannel.Help
data.value: (GLideN64) This should be enabled unless it's a old RICE Texture pack.

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-gliden64-EnableHiResAltCRC
data.value: Use alternative method for High-Res Checksums

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-gliden64-EnableHiResAltCRC.Help
data.value: (GLideN64) Use an alternative method for High-Res paletted textures CRC calculations.

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-gliden64-IniBehaviour.Help
data.value: (GLideN64) Specifies INI Settings behaviour. This should really only contain essential options. Changing this can and will break ROM's, if the correct options aren't set manually. Some options may only be set via INI (fbInfoDisabled).

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-gliden64-LegacySm64ToolsHacks
data.value: Patch SM64 Hacks made with SM64 Editor

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-gliden64-LegacySm64ToolsHacks.Help
data.value: (GLideN64) Make plugin behave like Jabo in certain case to fix compatibility with legacy SM64 hacks. It adds undocumented behavior that may interfere with real N64 games (unlikely).

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-gliden64-RemoveFBBlackBars.Help
data.value: (GLideN64) Remove the black bars added by VI emulation of the FrameBuffer.

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-OverrideSaveType.Help
data.value: Sets the save type used by unknown ROMs

data.name: Emulation.Option.parallel_n64.parallel-n64-rtc-savestate
data.value: Rollback N64 system clock on savestate load

data.name: Emulation.Emulator.pokemini.Description
data.value: Emulates compatible Nintendo systems with PokeMini.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pokemini.pokemini_video_scale.Help
data.value: Set internal video scale factor. Increasing the scale factor improves the appearance of the internal 'Dot Matrix' LCD filter.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pokemini.pokemini_60hz_mode.Help
data.value: Update the display at 60Hz instead of the native 72Hz Pokemon Mini's refresh rate by dropping every sixth frame. Reduces video smoothness, but avoids screen tearing on displays that do not support native operation above 60Hz.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pokemini.pokemini_lcdfilter.Help
data.value: Select internal screen filter. 'Dot Matrix' produces an LCD effect that mimics real hardware. LCD filters are disabled when 'Video Scale' is set to '1x'.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pokemini.pokemini_lcdmode.Help
data.value: Specify the greyscale 'color' reproduction characteristics of the emulated liquid crystal display. 'Analog' mimics real hardware. '2 Shades' removes ghosting, but causes flickering in most games.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pokemini.pokemini_lcdcontrast.Help
data.value: Set contrast level of emulated liquid crystal display.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pokemini.pokemini_lcdbright.Help
data.value: Set brightness offset of emulated liquid crystal display.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pokemini.pokemini_palette.Help
data.value: Specify palette used to 'colorize' the emulated liquid crystal display. 'Default' mimics real hardware.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pokemini.pokemini_piezofilter.Help
data.value: Use an audio filter to simulate the characteristics of the Pokemon Mini's piezoelectric speaker.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pokemini.pokemini_lowpass_filter.Help
data.value: Enables a low pass audio filter to soften the 'harsh' sound of the Pokemon Mini's piezoelectric speaker.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pokemini.pokemini_lowpass_range.Help
data.value: Specifies the cut-off frequency of the low pass audio filter. A higher value increases the perceived 'strength' of the filter, since a wider range of the high frequency spectrum is attenuated.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pokemini.pokemini_screen_shake_lv.Help
data.value: Enable virtual force feedback effect by 'shaking' the screen.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pokemini.pokemini_rumble_lv.Help
data.value: Enable physical force feedback effect via controller rumble.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pokemini.pokemini_turbo_period.Help
data.value: Specify the repeat interval (in frames) when holding down the Turbo A button.

data.name: Emulation.Emulator.mednafen_snes.Description
data.value: Emulates compatible Nintendo systems with Beetle SNES.

data.name: Emulation.Emulator.bsnes.Description
data.value: Emulates compatible Nintendo systems with bsnes.

data.name: Emulation.Option.bsnes.bsnes_aspect_ratio.Help
data.value: Choose the preferred content aspect ratio. This will only apply when RetroArch's aspect ratio is set to 'Core provided' in the Video settings.

data.name: Emulation.Option.bsnes.bsnes_ppu_overscan_v.Help
data.value: Remove N lines from the top and bottom of the screen to simulate the bezel of a television of the SNES era.

data.name: Emulation.Option.bsnes.bsnes_blur_emulation.Help
data.value: Simulate the limited horizontal resolution of SDTVs by blurring together horizontally-adjacent pixels. Some games depend on this to emulate a transparency effect.

data.name: Emulation.Option.bsnes.bsnes_video_filter.Help
data.value: Choose between no filtering and blargg's NTSC filter with options for RF, Composite, S-Video, or RGB

data.name: Emulation.Option.bsnes.bsnes_ppu_fast.Help
data.value: Enable faster emulation of the PPU at the cost of a minor reduction of accuracy. It is recommended to leave this on. NOTE: this must be enabled for the 'Deinterlace', 'No Sprite Limit' and the 'HD Mode 7' options to work.

data.name: Emulation.Option.bsnes.bsnes_ppu_deinterlace.Help
data.value: Deinterlace all games by rendering internally at 480p. Performance penalty is almost non-existent, so it is recommended to leave this on.

data.name: Emulation.Option.bsnes.bsnes_ppu_no_sprite_limit.Help
data.value: Remove any limit to the number of sprites that can be drawn simultaneously on screen. May cause issues with some games.

data.name: Emulation.Option.bsnes.bsnes_ppu_no_vram_blocking.Help
data.value: Emulate a bug in older releases of ZSNES and Snes9x, where VRAM blocking was not emulated. A few older ROM hacks relied on this behavior and will render graphics incorrectly if this is not enabled. This option is extremely inaccurate and hurts PPU speed, so it is recommended to leave it disabled unless you need to play a game that is otherwise incompatible with this core.

data.name: Emulation.Option.bsnes.bsnes_mode7_scale.Help

data.name: Emulation.Option.bsnes.bsnes_mode7_mosaic.Help

data.name: Emulation.Option.bsnes_hd_beta.bsnes_mode7_windRad.Help

data.name: Emulation.Option.bsnes_hd_beta.bsnes_mode7_widescreen.Help

data.name: Emulation.Option.bsnes_hd_beta.bsnes_mode7_wsbg1.Help

data.name: Emulation.Option.bsnes_hd_beta.bsnes_mode7_wsBgCol.Help

data.name: Emulation.Option.bsnes_hd_beta.bsnes_mode7_igwinx.Help

data.name: Emulation.Option.bsnes_hd_beta.bsnes_mode7_wsMarker.Help

data.name: Emulation.Option.bsnes_hd_beta.bsnes_mode7_wsMarkerAlpha.Help
data.value: If widescreen markers are enabled, this option allows to specify their translucency.

data.name: Emulation.Option.bsnes_hd_beta.bsnes_mode7_strWin.Help
data.value: Extends windowing effects into the widescreen areas at the cost of precision. It is recommended to keep this option disabled, unless needed for widescreen hacks.

data.name: Emulation.Option.snes9x.snes9x_region.Help
data.value: Specify which region the system is from. 'PAL' is 50hz, 'NTSC' is 60hz. Games will run faster or slower than normal if the incorrect region is selected.

data.name: Emulation.Option.snes9x.snes9x_aspect.Help
data.value: Choose the preferred content aspect ratio. This will only apply when RetroArch's aspect ratio is set to 'Core provided' in the Video settings.

data.name: Emulation.Option.snes9x.snes9x_overscan.Help
data.value: Remove the borders at the top and bottom of the screen, typically unused by games and hidden by the bezel of a standard-definition television. 'Auto' will attempt to detect and crop the ~8 pixel overscan based on the current content.

data.name: Emulation.Option.snes9x.snes9x_mode7_hires.Help
data.value: Render Mode 7 backgrounds at a higher horizontal resolution. 2x/4x sample the rotation matrix at sub-pixel steps; the _hv variants additionally resample vertically for square pixels. From snes9x2010.

data.name: Emulation.Option.snes9x.snes9x_mode7_hires_bilinear.Help
data.value: Texture sampling filter for HD Mode 7. 'Stable' bilinear snaps to texel centres to avoid shimmer; 'Smooth' is full bilinear.

data.name: Emulation.Option.snes9x.snes9x_hires_blend.Help
data.value: Blend adjacent pixels when game switches to hi-res mode (512x448). Required for certain games that use hi-res mode to produce transparency effects (Kirby's Dream Land, Jurassic Park...).

data.name: Emulation.Option.snes9x.snes9x_blargg.Help
data.value: Apply a video filter to mimic various NTSC TV signals.

data.name: Emulation.Option.snes9x.snes9x_audio_interpolation.Help
data.value: Apply an audio filter. 'Gaussian' reproduces the bass-heavy sound of the original hardware. 'Cubic' and 'Sinc' are less accurate, and preserve more of the high range.

data.name: Emulation.Option.snes9x.snes9x_up_down_allowed.Help
data.value: Enabling this will allow pressing / quickly alternating / holding both left and right (or up and down) directions at the same time. This may cause movement-based glitches.

data.name: Emulation.Option.snes9x.snes9x_overclock_superfx.Help
data.value: SuperFX coprocessor frequency multiplier. Can improve frame rate or cause timing errors. Values under 100% can improve game performance on slow devices.

data.name: Emulation.Option.snes9x.snes9x_superfx_timing.Help
data.value: 'Compatibility' runs the GSU with snes9x2010's field-tested per-line budget. 'Hardware-derived' charges each instruction its approximate real GSU cycle cost (cache-aware fetches, 5-cycle memory accesses, amortized plot flushes), matching ares/MiSTer wait states; backported from mainline Snes9x. More accurate, less field-tested. Works together with SuperFX Overclocking.

data.name: Emulation.Option.snes9x.snes9x_overclock_cycles.Help
data.value: Overclock SNES CPU. May cause games to crash! Use 'Light' for shorter loading times, 'Compatible' for most games exhibiting slowdown and 'Max' only if absolutely required (Gradius 3, Super R-type...).

data.name: Emulation.Option.snes9x.snes9x_reduce_sprite_flicker.Help
data.value: Increases number of sprites that can be drawn simultaneously on screen.

data.name: Emulation.Option.snes9x.snes9x_randomize_memory.Help
data.value: Randomizes system RAM upon start-up. Some games such as 'Super Off Road' use system RAM as a random number generator for item placement and AI behavior, to make gameplay more unpredictable.

data.name: Emulation.Option.snes9x.snes9x_block_invalid_vram_access.Help
data.value: Some homebrew/ROM hacks require this option to be disabled for correct operation.

data.name: Emulation.Option.snes9x.snes9x_echo_buffer_hack
data.value: Echo Buffer Hack (Unsafe, only enable for old addmusic hacks)

data.name: Emulation.Option.snes9x.snes9x_echo_buffer_hack.Help
data.value: Some homebrew/ROM hacks require this option to be enabled for correct operation.

data.name: Emulation.Option.snes9x.snes9x_show_lightgun_settings.Help
data.value: Enable configuration of Super Scope / Justifier / M.A.C.S. rifle input. NOTE: Quick Menu must be toggled for this setting to take effect.

data.name: Emulation.Option.snes9x.snes9x_lightgun_mode.Help

data.name: Emulation.Option.snes9x.snes9x_superscope_reverse_buttons.Help
data.value: Swap the positions of the Super Scope 'Fire' and 'Cursor' buttons.

data.name: Emulation.Option.snes9x.snes9x_superscope_crosshair.Help
data.value: Change the crosshair size on screen.

data.name: Emulation.Option.snes9x.snes9x_superscope_color.Help
data.value: Change the crosshair color on screen.

data.name: Emulation.Option.snes9x.snes9x_justifier1_crosshair.Help
data.value: Change the crosshair size on screen.

data.name: Emulation.Option.snes9x.snes9x_justifier1_color.Help
data.value: Change the crosshair color on screen.

data.name: Emulation.Option.snes9x.snes9x_justifier2_crosshair.Help
data.value: Change the crosshair size on screen.

data.name: Emulation.Option.snes9x.snes9x_justifier2_color.Help
data.value: Change the crosshair color on screen.

data.name: Emulation.Option.snes9x.snes9x_rifle_crosshair.Help
data.value: Change the crosshair size on screen.

data.name: Emulation.Option.snes9x.snes9x_rifle_color.Help
data.value: Change the crosshair color on screen.

data.name: Emulation.Option.snes9x.snes9x_msu1_enhanced_audio.Help
data.value: Run the audio pipeline at 44.1 kHz when an MSU-1 game is loaded. When disabled, MSU-1's 44.1 kHz PCM stream is decimated to the SNES's native ~32 kHz output with no anti-alias filtering, folding the track's top octave into the audible band as slight hiss. When enabled, the MSU-1 stream passes through bit-exactly and the SPC sound is upsampled cleanly. Has no effect on non-MSU-1 games. Changing this takes effect on the next content load.

data.name: Emulation.Option.snes9x.snes9x_show_advanced_av_settings.Help

data.value: Emulates compatible Nintendo systems with Snes9x 2002.

data.name: Emulation.Option.snes9x2002.snes9x2002_frameskip.Help
data.value: Skip frames to avoid audio buffer under-run (crackling). Improves performance at the expense of visual smoothness. 'Auto' skips frames when advised by the frontend. 'Auto (Threshold)' utilises the 'Frameskip Threshold (%)' setting. 'Fixed Interval' utilises the 'Frameskip Interval' setting.

data.name: Emulation.Option.snes9x2002.snes9x2002_frameskip_threshold.Help
data.value: When 'Frameskip' is set to 'Auto (Threshold)', specifies the audio buffer occupancy threshold (percentage) below which frames will be skipped. Higher values reduce the risk of crackling by causing frames to be dropped more frequently.

data.name: Emulation.Option.snes9x2002.snes9x2002_frameskip_interval.Help
data.value: When 'Frameskip' is set to 'Fixed Interval', the value set here is the number of frames omitted after a frame is rendered - i.e. '0' = 60fps, '1' = 30fps, '2' = 15fps, etc.

data.name: Emulation.Option.snes9x2002.snes9x2002_transparency.Help
data.value: Disable to improve frame rate at the expense of rendering accuracy.

data.name: Emulation.Option.snes9x2002.snes9x2002_low_pass_filter.Help
data.value: Enable a low pass audio filter to soften treble artifacts and mimic the 'bassy' sound of original SNES hardware.

data.name: Emulation.Option.snes9x2002.snes9x2002_low_pass_range.Help
data.value: Specify the cut-off frequency of the low pass audio filter. A higher value increases the perceived 'strength' of the filter, since a wider range of the high frequency spectrum is attenuated.

data.value: Specify which region the system is from. 'PAL' is 50hz, 'NTSC' is 60hz. Games will run faster or slower than normal if the incorrect region is selected.

data.name: Emulation.Option.snes9x2010.snes9x_2010_audio_interpolation.Help
data.value: Choose how each SNES voice's pitch is interpolated. 'Gaussian' matches real hardware. 'Cubic' is brighter and less muffled, but does not match hardware and does not undo BRR sample compression. 'Sinc' is the sharpest/brightest (8-tap) and the most CPU-intensive.

data.name: Emulation.Option.snes9x2010.snes9x_2010_msu1_enhanced_audio.Help
data.value: Run the entire audio pipeline at 44.1 kHz for MSU-1 games. When disabled, MSU-1's 44.1 kHz PCM stream is decimated to the SNES's native ~32 kHz before output with no anti-alias filtering, folding the track's top octave into the audible band as slight hiss. When enabled, the SPC sound is resampled up to 44.1 kHz and the MSU-1 stream passes through bit-exactly at its native rate. Has no effect on non-MSU-1 games. Changing this takes effect on the next content load.

data.name: Emulation.Option.snes9x2010.snes9x_2010_threaded_ppu.Help
data.value: Draw the picture on a second thread, a scanline range at a time, while the CPU runs on. Output is identical either way. Worth it where there is a spare core to draw on; on a single-core machine it only adds the cost of handing work across. Changing this takes effect on the next content load.

data.name: Emulation.Option.snes9x2010.snes9x_2010_aspect.Help
data.value: Choose the preferred content aspect ratio. This will only apply when RetroArch's aspect ratio is set to 'Core provided' in the Video settings.

data.name: Emulation.Option.snes9x2010.snes9x_2010_blargg.Help

data.name: Emulation.Option.snes9x2010.snes9x_2010_frameskip.Help

data.name: Emulation.Option.snes9x2010.snes9x_2010_frameskip_threshold.Help
data.value: When 'Frameskip' is set to 'Manual', specifies the audio buffer occupancy threshold (percentage) below which frames will be skipped. Higher values reduce the risk of crackling by causing frames to be dropped more frequently.

data.name: Emulation.Option.snes9x2010.snes9x_2010_overclock.Help
data.value: Overclock or underclock the SuperFX chip. This may improve the framerate and playability of games that use SuperFX.

data.name: Emulation.Option.snes9x2010.snes9x_2010_overclock_cycles.Help
data.value: Overclock SNES CPU. May cause games to crash! Use 'Light' for shorter loading times, 'Compatible' for most games exhibiting slowdown and 'Max' only if absolutely required (Gradius 3, Super R-type...).

data.name: Emulation.Option.snes9x2010.snes9x_2010_superfx_timing.Help
data.value: 'Legacy' keeps the shipped per-line budgets (including the cycle-accuracy toggle below). 'Hardware-derived' charges each instruction its approximate real GSU cycle cost (cache-aware fetches, 5-cycle memory accesses, amortized plot flushes), matching ares/MiSTer wait states; backported from mainline Snes9x. When set to 'Hardware-derived', the cycle-accuracy toggle is ignored. Works together with the SuperFX Overclock option.

data.name: Emulation.Option.snes9x2010.snes9x_2010_superfx_cycle_accuracy.Help
data.value: Charge each SuperFX (GSU) instruction an approximate hardware cycle cost (multiplies, RAM/ROM access, plots) rather than a flat per-instruction budget, for more hardware-like GSU timing. Set to 'disabled' for the legacy instruction-count behaviour. Works together with the SuperFX overclock option.

data.name: Emulation.Option.snes9x2010.snes9x_2010_reduce_sprite_flicker.Help
data.value: Increases number of sprites that can be drawn simultaneously on screen.

data.name: Emulation.Option.snes9x2010.snes9x_2010_block_invalid_vram_access.Help
data.value: Some homebrew/ROM hacks require this option to be disabled for correct operation.

data.name: Emulation.Option.snes9x2010.snes9x_2010_mode7_hires.Help
data.value: Render Mode 7 backgrounds at higher resolution. 2x renders at 512 px (smoother diagonals); 4x renders at 1024 px (smoothest, more expensive). The 2x_hv / 4x_hv variants additionally double the output vertically (448 rows) via an end-of-frame bilinear-Y average of adjacent rendered rows; HUD / sprites / non-M7 layers are row-duplicated. Smooths row-to-row transitions on Mode 7 ground textures but does not add per-line detail (the M7 plane still samples at 224 source rows). Affects only Mode 7 (driving / racing / overhead-rotation games). Other modes are unchanged. Default off.

data.name: Emulation.Option.snes9x2010.snes9x_2010_mode7_hires_bilinear.Help
data.value: Apply bilinear filtering to Mode 7 backgrounds. Stable: blends along the X axis only with floor-Y sampling. Robust against high-contrast horizontal banding (rainbow rings, palette-rotation effects); recommended default. Smooth: 4-corner bilinear with a row-contrast guard that falls back to stable behaviour on high-contrast row pairs (avoids muddy seams on content like the Tiny Toons title screen). More aggressive smoothing along both axes; somewhat more expensive than stable. Independent of the Hires option; works at native, 2x and 4x.

data.name: Emulation.Option.snes9x2010.snes9x_2010_pseudo_hires_blend.Help
data.value: Blends adjacent column pairs in pseudo-hires frames to reproduce the composite-video softening that some games rely on for fake transparency effects (waterfalls, glass, fog: Kirby's Dream Land 3, Jurassic Park). Applies a 2-tap horizontal average to the finished 512 px frame while keeping the full hires resolution; it does not reduce the image to 256 px. Affects only frames that actually use pseudo-hires; native and true Mode 5/6 hires output is unchanged. Ignored when the Blargg NTSC filter is active, since that already simulates the same softening. Default off.

data.name: Emulation.Option.cemu.cemu_cpu_mode.Help
data.value: How the Wii U's PowerPC cores are emulated. Auto takes the multicore recompiler on a CPU with four or more physical cores and the single-core one otherwise. The interpreters are far slower and are meant for debugging. (Restart required)

data.name: Emulation.Option.cemu.cemu_show_game_fps.Help
data.value: Show the frame rate the game renders at. RetroArch's own FPS counter counts how often the core runs, and that stays at 60 when the game drops frames, because every run carries a frame's worth of audio.

data.name: Emulation.Option.cemu.cemu_internal_resolution.Help
data.value: A generic fallback for games without a resolution graphic pack: resizes every screen-shaped render target, which some games use for things that break when resized. 640x360 draws a quarter of the pixels of 720p. When a resolution pack is enabled for the loaded game (Graphic Packs), the pack sets the resolution and this option is hidden.

data.name: Emulation.Option.cemu.cemu_rumble_strength.Help
data.value: How strongly the controller vibrates when the game asks for it: the GamePad's motor, and the Wii Remote's or Pro Controller's. Off sends the frontend no rumble at all.

data.name: Emulation.Option.cemu.cemu_dump_shaders.Help
data.value: Writes the source of every shader the game uses to system/Cemu/dump/shaders, named by its hashes as they appear in log.txt. For reporting a shader that fails or draws wrongly on a particular GPU. Slows shader compilation down and fills the folder quickly, so turn it off again afterwards.

data.name: Emulation.Option.cemu.cemu_log_texture_memory.Help
data.value: Reports how much of the texture memory is BC that had to be decompressed because this GPU cannot sample it.

data.name: Emulation.Option.cemu.cemu_log_input_api.Help
data.value: Logs every controller call a title makes - which pads it probed for and what it was told. Noisy; for a few seconds at a time.

data.name: Emulation.Option.cemu.cemu_log_audio.Help
data.value: Once a second, how many samples AX produced, how many the ring had to drop, and how many the frontend took. For working out which end of that chain audio is going missing at.

data.name: Emulation.Option.cemu.cemu_bc1_16bit.Help
data.value: Halves what BC1 textures cost on a GPU that cannot sample BC, at the price of one bit of green. No effect where BC is supported.

data.name: Emulation.Option.cemu.cemu_gpu_api.Help
data.value: The graphics API Cemu renders with. (Restart required)

data.name: Emulation.Option.cemu.cemu_install_game.Help
data.value:
Installs every game in system/Cemu/titles into saves/Cemu/mlc01, the emulated console's storage, as the console installs a game from its disc. A game is a disc image (.wud, .wux, .iso) or a .wua, and from a .wua the update and DLC it holds are installed with it. A game installed already in the same or a newer version is left alone.
When this is ON, installing begins immediately, with its progress shown as a notification, and it turns OFF again when all games are installed. An installed game is started by loading the .rpx in its code folder, under mlc01/usr/title/00050000; its disc image is not needed any more.

data.name: Emulation.Option.cemu.cemu_uninstall_game.Help
data.value: Uninstalls the running game from saves/Cemu/mlc01 once the game is closed or reset, together with its installed update and DLC; it stays on until then. Its saves are left alone, as are the disc image or .wua it was installed from.

data.name: Emulation.Option.cemu.cemu_install_titles.Help
data.value:
Installs every update and DLC in system/Cemu/titles into saves/Cemu/mlc01, the emulated console's storage. Each one goes in a folder of its own there; a NUS download (.app files) needs its title.tmd and its title.tik, the decryption key, next to them. A version already installed that is the same or newer is left alone.
When this is ON, installing begins immediately, with its progress shown as a notification, and it turns OFF again when all content is installed and this menu is exited or another option is changed. The title will use the installed content once it is restarted.
Content from other locations can be installed with RetroArch's Main Menu > Load Content, by selecting the corresponding title.tmd, with its title.tik beside it.

data.name: Emulation.Option.cemu.cemu_uninstall_titles.Help
data.value: Uninstalls the running game's update and DLC from saves/Cemu/mlc01, the emulated console's storage, once the game is closed or reset; it stays on until then. Copies in system/Cemu/titles are left alone.

data.name: Emulation.Option.cemu.cemu_install_remove_source.Help
data.value:
Removes downloadable content and title updates from system/Cemu/titles once Install Content has installed them. Content loaded through Load Content is left where it is.
The running title's update or DLC is in use, so it is removed when the title is closed or reset.
.wua files and disc images are never removed, as they can hold the base game as well.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mupen64plus-next.mupen64plus-EnableLODEmulation.Help

data.name: Emulation.Option.mupen64plus-next.mupen64plus-EnableCopyDepthToRDRAM.Help

data.name: Emulation.Option.mupen64plus-next.mupen64plus-BackgroundMode.Help

data.name: Emulation.Option.mupen64plus-next.mupen64plus-EnableHWLighting.Help
data.value: (GLN64) Standard per-vertex lighting when disabled. Slightly different rendering.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mupen64plus-next.mupen64plus-CorrectTexrectCoords.Help
data.value: (GLN64) Make texrect coordinates continuous to avoid black lines between them.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mupen64plus-next.mupen64plus-EnableInaccurateTextureCoordinates.Help
data.value: (GLN64) Enables inaccurate texture coordinate calculations. This can improve performance and texture pack compatibity at the cost of accuracy.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mupen64plus-next.mupen64plus-EnableTexCoordBounds

data.name: Emulation.Option.mupen64plus-next.mupen64plus-EnableTexCoordBounds.Help

data.name: Emulation.Option.mupen64plus-next.mupen64plus-EnableFragmentDepthWrite.Help

data.name: Emulation.Option.mupen64plus-next.mupen64plus-EnableN64DepthCompare.Help
data.value: (GLN64) Enable N64 depth compare instead of OpenGL standard one. Experimental, Fast mode will have more glitches.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mupen64plus-next.mupen64plus-EnableShadersStorage.Help
data.value: (GLN64) Use persistent storage for compiled shaders.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mupen64plus-next.mupen64plus-EnableTextureCache.Help

data.name: Emulation.Option.mupen64plus-next.mupen64plus-EnableOverscan.Help

data.name: Emulation.Option.mupen64plus-next.mupen64plus-MaxHiResTxVramLimit.Help

data.name: Emulation.Option.mupen64plus-next.mupen64plus-MaxTxCacheSize.Help

data.name: Emulation.Option.mupen64plus-next.mupen64plus-txEnhancementMode.Help

data.name: Emulation.Option.mupen64plus-next.mupen64plus-txHiresEnable.Help

data.name: Emulation.Option.mupen64plus-next.mupen64plus-txHiresFullAlphaChannel.Help

data.name: Emulation.Option.mupen64plus-next.mupen64plus-EnableEnhancedHighResStorage.Help

data.name: Emulation.Option.mupen64plus-next.mupen64plus-parallel-rdp-synchronous.Help

data.name: Emulation.Option.mupen64plus-next.mupen64plus-parallel-rdp-overscan.Help

data.name: Emulation.Option.mupen64plus-next.mupen64plus-parallel-rdp-divot-filter.Help

data.name: Emulation.Option.mupen64plus-next.mupen64plus-virefresh.Help
data.value: Select a VI Refresh clock, Auto does not impact behaviour, other values override CountPerScanline.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mupen64plus-next.mupen64plus-ForceDisableExtraMem.Help
data.value: Force disable Expansion Pak (might improve performance for some games while reducing emulation accuracy, will break games that require it).

data.name: Emulation.Option.mupen64plus-next.mupen64plus-IgnoreTLBExceptions.Help
data.value: (HACK) Ignore emulated TLB Exceptions, this might fix some broken romhacks. This option might be removed in the future.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mupen64plus-next.mupen64plus-IgnoreTLBExceptions.Value.OnlyNotEnabled
data.value: Ignore TLB Exceptions if not using TLB

data.name: Emulation.Option.mupen64plus-next.mupen64plus-CountPerOp.Help
data.value: Count per Op is used to approximate the Counter reg, 0 will use the embedded Database (or default to 2). Changing this will break stuff!

data.name: Emulation.Option.mupen64plus-next.mupen64plus-CountPerOpDenomPot.Help
data.value: Denominator for Count per Op (allowing sub-1 Count per Op in practice). Changing this can break stuff!

data.name: Emulation.Option.mupen64plus-next.mupen64plus-astick-deadzone.Help
data.value: Size of the non responsive area around an analog stick.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mupen64plus-next.mupen64plus-astick-sensitivity.Help
data.value: Adjust how far the stick needs to be moved to reach its max value.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mupen64plus-next.mupen64plus-alt-map.Help
data.value: Use an alternate control scheme, useful for some 3rdparty controllers.

data.name: Emulation.Option.beetle_vb.vb_3dmode.Help
data.value: Select the 3D mode. Anaglyph - used in conjunction with classic dual-lens-color glasses. Cyberscope - intended for use with the CyberScope 3D device. sidebyside - the left-eye image is displayed on the left, and the right-eye image is displayed on the right. vli - Vertical lines alternate between left and right view. hli - Horizontal lines alternate between left and right view.

data.name: Emulation.Option.beetle_vb.vb_sidebyside_separation.Help
data.value: Number of pixels to separate left and right views in side-by-side 3D mode.

data.name: Emulation.Option.beetle_vb.vb_opposite_directions.Help
data.value: Allow pressing up and down or left and right directions at the same time. This may cause glitches.

data.name: Emulation.Option.beetle_vb.vb_cpu_emulation.Help
data.value: Choose between faster and accurate (slower) emulation.
